title: The Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Antiviral Activity of ABI ‐4334, A Novel Next‐Generation Hepatitis B Capsid Assembly Modulator
abstract: ABSTRACT Novel, well‐tolerated, short‐term therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) are needed. ABI‐4334 is a next‐generation capsid assembly modulator that targets the HBV core protein. The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI‐4334 in healthy volunteers and participants with cHBV and antiviral effects in participants with cHBV were examined in two Phase 1 studies. Study 101 was a placebo‐controlled study of healthy volunteers that included four single‐ascending dose cohorts and two once‐daily multiple‐ascending dose cohorts randomized 6:2 (ABI‐4334:placebo), and one crossover food‐effect cohort randomized 3:3 (fed:fasted). Study 102 was a randomized, blinded, placebo‐controlled study where participants with cHBV were randomized 8:2 (ABI‐4334 [2 dose cohorts]:placebo). Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively. Most participants (75%) in Study 102 were hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) negative and generally had lower baseline HBV DNA and pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) levels. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with no treatment‐emergent serious adverse events (AEs) or treatment‐emergent AEs leading to study discontinuation. The mean ABI‐4334 plasma half‐life ranges were comparable across doses in both studies. Following multiple‐dose administration in participants with cHBV, the steady‐state mean plasma half‐life ranged from 17.5 to 27.5 h. HBV DNA declines were observed in both HBeAg‐positive ( n = 3) and ‐negative ( n = 13) participants across doses. Reductions in pgRNA were observed in participants with detectable pgRNA at baseline. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with pharmacokinetics and antiviral results supporting the continued development of ABI‐4334 as a monotherapy or component of novel combination regimens for cHBV. Trial Registration: Study 101 (NCT05569941). Study 102 (NCT06384131)

source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Novel, well‐tolerated, short‐term therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) are needed. ABI‐4334 is a next‐generation capsid assembly modulator that targets the HBV core protein. The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI‐4334 in healthy volunteers and participants with cHBV and antiviral effects in participants with cHBV were examined in two Phase 1 studies. Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively. Following multiple‐dose administration in participants with cHBV, the steady‐state mean plasma half‐life ranged from 17.5 to 27.5 h. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 进行了两项 1 期研究:研究 101 涉及健康志愿者,接受四名单次递增剂量 队列研究 和两次每日一次多次递增剂量 队列研究,而研究 102 涉及 cHBV 随机 8:2 受试者(ABI-4334 [2 剂量 队列研究]:安慰剂)。总体而言,研究 101 和研究 102 分别纳入了 54 名健康志愿者和 20 名患有 cHBV 的参与者。
elements_zh.methods: ABI-4334 的安全性、耐受性和药代动力学在两项 1 期研究中进行了检查。在研究101中,使用单次和多次递增剂量队列研究的安慰剂对照设计,在研究102中,实施随机、盲法、安慰剂对照设计。
elements_zh.main_results: 在不同剂量的 HBeAg 阳性 (n = 3) 和阴性 (n = 13) 参与者中均观察到 HBV DNA 下降。此外,基线时可检测到 pgRNA 的参与者的 pgRNA 有所减少。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The studies were Phase 1 trials with limited sample sizes, which may restrict the generalizability of the findings. However, the evidence is strong given the consistent pharmacokinetic profiles and antiviral activity observed.

title_zh: 新型下一代乙型肝炎衣壳组装调节剂 ABI ‐4334 的安全性、药代动力学和 抗病毒药物 活性
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Novel, well‐tolerated, short‐term therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) are needed. ABI‐4334 is a next‐generation capsid assembly modulator that targets the HBV core protein. The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI‐4334 in healthy volunteers and participants with cHBV and antiviral effects in participants with cHBV were examined in two Phase 1 studies. Study 101 was a placebo‐controlled study of healthy volunteers that included four single‐ascending dose cohorts and two once‐daily multiple‐ascending dose cohorts randomized 6:2 (ABI‐4334:placebo), and one crossover food‐effect cohort randomized 3:3 (fed:fasted). Study 102 was a randomized, blinded, placebo‐controlled study where participants with cHBV were randomized 8:2 (ABI‐4334 [2 dose cohorts]:placebo). Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively. Most participants (75%) in Study 102 were hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) negative and generally had lower baseline HBV DNA and pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) levels. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with no treatment‐emergent serious adverse events (AEs) or treatment‐emergent AEs leading to study discontinuation. The mean ABI‐4334 plasma half‐life ranges were comparable across doses in both studies. Following multiple‐dose administration in participants with cHBV, the steady‐state mean plasma half‐life ranged from 17.5 to 27.5 h. HBV DNA declines were observed in both HBeAg‐positive ( n = 3) and ‐negative ( n = 13) participants across doses. Reductions in pgRNA were observed in participants with detectable pgRNA at baseline. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with pharmacokinetics and antiviral results supporting the continued development of ABI‐4334 as a monotherapy or component of novel combination regimens for cHBV. Trial Registration: Study 101 (NCT05569941). Study 102 (NCT06384131)

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为了解 ABI-4334 作为治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染的新治疗选择的潜力提供了重要见解,这可以为未来的临床试验和 治疗 策略提供信息。

title: The dual role of protein glycosylation in HBV infection: facilitating viral pathogenesis and shaping host defense
abstract: Hepatitis B is the most prevalent chronic viral infection worldwide, posing a serious threat to global public health. Protein glycosylation, a critical post-translational modification, regulates diverse physiological processes. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with altered glycosylation of both viral and host proteins, which influences viral entry, immune evasion and disease progression, while HBV infection remodels host glycosylation. Given the sensitivity of glycosylation patterns to pathological perturbations, it is particularly relevant to examine how HBV exploits host glycosylation machinery to facilitate viral persistence and pathogenesis. This review is organised around a dual-role framework: one arm covers the proviral functions of glycosylation (viral entry, envelope protein folding, processing, assembly and secretion, persistence, immune escape and disease progression), the other the host-protective functions of the same pathways (glycosylation-dependent restriction factors, glycan-dependent ER quality control and ERAD, cellular stress responses and immune regulation). This exploration provides insights into the glycan-dependent mechanisms underlying HBV infection and their implications for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title_zh: 蛋白质糖基化在 HBV 感染中的双重作用:促进病毒 发病机制 和塑造 宿主 防御
source_body_en: Hepatitis B is the most prevalent chronic viral infection worldwide, posing a serious threat to global public health. Protein glycosylation, a critical post-translational modification, regulates diverse physiological processes. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with altered glycosylation of both viral and host proteins, which influences viral entry, immune evasion and disease progression, while HBV infection remodels host glycosylation. Given the sensitivity of glycosylation patterns to pathological perturbations, it is particularly relevant to examine how HBV exploits host glycosylation machinery to facilitate viral persistence and pathogenesis. This review is organised around a dual-role framework: one arm covers the proviral functions of glycosylation (viral entry, envelope protein folding, processing, assembly and secretion, persistence, immune escape and disease progression), the other the host-protective functions of the same pathways (glycosylation-dependent restriction factors, glycan-dependent ER quality control and ERAD, cellular stress responses and immune regulation). This exploration provides insights into the glycan-dependent mechanisms underlying HBV infection and their implications for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎是全球最流行的慢性病毒感染,对全球公共卫生构成严重威胁。蛋白质糖基化是一种关键的翻译后修饰,调节多种生理过程。乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染与病毒和 宿主 蛋白的糖基化改变有关,这会影响病毒进入、免疫逃避和疾病进展,而 HBV 感染会重塑 宿主 糖基化。考虑到糖基化模式对病理扰动的敏感性,检查 HBV 如何利用 宿主 糖基化机制来促进病毒持久性和 发病机制 尤为重要。本综述围绕双重角色框架进行组织:一方面涵盖糖基化的原病毒功能(病毒进入、包膜蛋白折叠、加工、组装和分泌、持久性、免疫逃逸和疾病进展),另一方面涵盖相同途径的 宿主 保护功能(糖基化依赖性限制因子、聚糖依赖性 ER 质量控制和 ERAD、细胞应激反应和免疫调节)。这项探索提供了对 HBV 感染背后的聚糖依赖性机制及其对开发新的诊断和治疗策略的影响的见解。

title: Hepatitis B and D: Interferon-Based Therapy-For Clinical Trials or Standard of Care-Back to the Future?
abstract: Interferon (IFN) has historically played a major role in chronic viral hepatitis B and D management over the last three decades. Widening utilisation of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) for hepatitis B viral suppression, which have a better side-effect profile, alongside the recent licensing of bulevirtide for treatment of hepatitis D, means that its clinical use has further declined. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) treatment is suboptimal with poor tolerability and achieves durable clearance of hepatitis B and D in only a limited number of patients. Nevertheless, its use in hepatitis B has significantly increased the number of patients achieving hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss compared to those on NUCs alone. Evidence has shown that peg-IFNα is also associated with overall improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, even for the many whose hepatitis D viral load rebounds after discontinuation. Clinical trials have recently focused on peg-IFNα in combination with novel antiviral therapies in the goal for finite cure in hepatitis B and D. This article focuses on recent research advances, examining if peg-IFNα treatment may still play an important role in hepatitis B and D treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the historical and current role of interferon-based therapy in managing hepatitis B and D. It highlights the decline in clinical use due to the availability of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) and bulevirtide, which offer better side-effect profiles. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) is noted as suboptimal with poor tolerability and limited durable clearance rates. However, its use in hepatitis B has increased HBsAg loss compared to NUCs alone. Additionally, peg-IFNα is associated with improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, despite viral load rebounds post-treatment. The review focuses on recent research advances and the potential for peg-IFNα to still play an important role in treatment strategies.

title_zh: 乙型和丁型肝炎:基于干扰素的治疗 - 用于临床试验或标准护理 - 回到未来?

abstract_zh: 过去三十年来,干扰素 (IFN) 在慢性病毒性乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎的治疗中发挥了重要作用。核苷/核苷酸类似物(NUC)在抑制乙型肝炎病毒方面的广泛应用(其副作用较小),加上最近获得的用于丁型肝炎 治疗 的 bulevirtide 许可,意味着其临床使用进一步下降。聚乙二醇化干扰素α (peg-IFNα) 治疗 效果欠佳,耐受性差,仅在有限数量的患者中实现了乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎的持久清除。尽管如此,与单独使用 NUC 的患者相比,其在乙型肝炎中的使用显着增加了实现乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 消失的患者数量。有证据表明,peg-IFNα 还与慢性丁型肝炎的长期临床结果的整体改善相关,即使对于许多丁型肝炎病毒载量在停药后反弹的人来说也是如此。最近的临床试验重点关注 peg-IFNα 与新型 抗病毒药物 疗法的联合治疗,以实现乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎的有限治愈。本文重点介绍最新的研究进展,探讨 peg-IFNα 治疗 是否仍可能在乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎 治疗 中发挥重要作用。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 聚乙二醇化干扰素α (peg-IFNα) 治疗 效果欠佳,耐受性差,仅在有限数量的患者中实现了乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎的持久清除。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 尽管如此,与单独使用 NUC 的患者相比,其在乙型肝炎中的使用显着增加了实现乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 消失的患者数量。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 有证据表明,peg-IFNα 还与慢性丁型肝炎的长期临床结果的整体改善相关,即使对于许多丁型肝炎病毒载量在停药后反弹的人来说也是如此。

title: Chronic Hepatitis B in the United States: Current Landscape, Unmet Needs and Future Directions.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection represents a major public health challenge in the US, with substantial unmet needs related to timely diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and disease management. This narrative review explores the CHB landscape in the US, including gaps in patient care, the evolving therapeutic landscape, the clinical utility of serological biomarkers to improve outcomes and the experiences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB). Hepatitis B remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in the US, and current efforts are insufficient to meet the associated World Health Organization 2030 elimination targets. Latest guidelines from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of America, representing a North American perspective, signify a shift towards expanded treatment eligibility criteria and shared decision-making. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) are the current standard of care in the US, but functional cure is rarely achieved with NAs alone. Novel finite therapies targeting functional cure, such as antisense oligonucleotides, small interfering RNAs, immune modulators and combination or sequential regimens, are under investigation. Because of the unpredictable, complex nature of CHB, biomarkers such as quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen offer prognostic value for treatment decisions and could help guide individualised CHB management. PLWHB experience psychological impacts and health-related concerns, including fear of transmission and hepatitis B virus-related complications. Opportunities for improvement of CHB management include increased screening and linkage to care, development of more treatments targeting functional cure, adoption of serological biomarkers to inform treatment decisions and prioritising the lived experiences and preferences of PLWHB.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights the significant public health challenge posed by chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in the United States, emphasizing the need for improved diagnosis, treatment, and disease management. The review outlines the current landscape of CHB, noting that it remains underdiagnosed and undertreated, with insufficient progress towards meeting WHO 2030 elimination targets. It discusses the limitations of nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) in achieving a functional cure and highlights the potential of novel therapies and serological biomarkers to improve outcomes. The review also underscores the importance of incorporating the lived experiences and preferences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB) into management strategies. These findings suggest a need for expanded treatment eligibility, shared decision-making, and further research into more effective therapeutic approaches.

abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 感染是美国的一项重大公共卫生挑战,与及时 诊断、治疗、监测和疾病管理相关的大量需求未得到满足。这篇叙述性综述探讨了美国慢性乙型肝炎的情况,包括患者护理方面的差距、不断发展的治疗前景、血清学生物标志物在改善乙型肝炎患者 (PLWHB) 患者的治疗结果和经历方面的临床效用。在美国,乙型肝炎的诊断和治疗仍然不足,目前的努力不足以实现世界卫生组织相关的 2030 年消除目标。美国肝病研究协会和美国传染病学会的最新指南代表了北美的观点,标志着向扩大 治疗 资格标准和共同决策的转变。核苷(酸)类似物 (NA) 是美国目前的护理标准,但单独使用 NA 很少能实现 功能性治愈。针对 功能性治愈 的新型有限疗法,例如反义寡核苷酸、小干扰 RNA、免疫调节剂以及组合或序贯疗法,正在研究中。由于慢性乙型肝炎的不可预测性和复杂性,定量乙型肝炎表面抗原等生物标志物可为 治疗 决策提供预后价值,并有助于指导个体化慢性乙型肝炎管理。PLWHB 经历心理影响和健康相关问题,包括对 传播 和 乙型肝炎病毒 相关并发症的恐惧。改善 CHB 管理的机会包括增加筛查和与护理的联系、开发更多针对 功能性治愈 的 治疗、采用血清学生物标志物来告知 治疗 决策以及优先考虑 PLWHB 的生活经历和偏好。

title: Multidisciplinary management of disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and active hepatitis B in a critically ill pregnant woman in the third trimester: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) in pregnancy is rare but life-threatening, with substantial maternal and fetal risks. Third-trimester disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system with concurrent active hepatitis B infection has scarcely been reported, particularly among remote pastoral populations with limited healthcare access. This report highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of this triple comorbidity and underscores the value of multidisciplinary team (MDT) management in such complex scenarios. Case presentation A 24-year-old pastoralist at 30 weeks of gestation presented with headache, vomiting, fever, and nuchal rigidity. Cerebrospinal fluidanalysis confirmed TBM, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication. Given life-threatening intracranial hypertension [intracranial pressure (ICP) > 330 mmH 2 O] in late pregnancy, osmotic agents were withheld for fetal safety, and lumbar cisternal drainage was performed. An MDT comprising respiratory medicine, obstetrics, hepatology, pharmacy, and critical care nursing specialties was assembled. Anti-tuberculosis therapy was intensified to isoniazid, rifampicin, linezolid, and moxifloxacin; ethambutol was discontinued due to fetal optic neuritis, and tenofovir was added for hepatitis B management. Following stabilization, the patient was transferred to a higher-level facility at 35 weeks of gestation and underwent cesarean section at 36 weeks, delivering a live preterm female infant (2320 g, 1-min Apgar score of 8). Both mother and neonate were discharged without complications on December 1, 2025. Conclusions This case demonstrates that early recognition, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimens, and coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration are critical for achieving favorable outcomes in pregnant patients with disseminated tuberculosis complicated by TBM and concurrent hepatitis B infection. The successful management relied on integrated critical care and a multidisciplinary approach, which proved effective even in resource-limited pastoral settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This case report addresses the challenges of diagnosing and managing disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and active hepatitis B in a critically ill pregnant woman, highlighting the need for awareness of such rare and complex comorbidities in clinical practice.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a case report of a 24-year-old pregnant woman in the third trimester who presented with headache, vomiting, fever, and nuchal rigidity, and was diagnosed with disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system and concurrent active hepatitis B infection.
analysis.methods: The diagnostic process included cerebrospinal fluid analysis and chest computed tomography to confirm tuberculous meningitis and disseminated tuberculosis. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of multidisciplinary approaches in managing rare and complex infections in pregnant women, particularly in resource-limited settings where such comorbidities may be under-recognized.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a single case report, which limits its generalizability. However, the evidence is strong for the specific case presented, given the detailed clinical and diagnostic information provided.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a rare and complex scenario of a 24-year-old pregnant woman in the third trimester who developed disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and active hepatitis B infection. The study highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of managing such a triple comorbidity, emphasizing the importance of early recognition, individualized treatment regimens, and coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration. The case underscores the value of integrated critical care in resource-limited pastoral settings. While the study is limited by its single-case design, the detailed clinical and diagnostic information provides strong evidence for the specific case and contributes to the understanding of managing overlapping infections in pregnant women. The findings have implications for improving surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies in similar clinical contexts.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一名24岁妊娠晚期孕妇的病例报告,她出现头痛、呕吐、发烧和颈项强直,被诊断为累及中枢神经系统的播散性结核病并并发活动性乙型肝炎感染。
elements_zh.methods: 诊断过程包括脑脊液分析和胸部计算机断层扫描,以确认结核性脑膜炎和播散性结核病。血清学 测试用于识别活动性乙型肝炎感染,治疗 涉及强化抗结核治疗方案,并针对胎儿安全进行调整。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This case report addresses the challenges of diagnosing and managing disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and active hepatitis B in a critically ill pregnant woman, highlighting the need for awareness of such rare and complex comorbidities in clinical practice.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a case report of a 24-year-old pregnant woman in the third trimester who presented with headache, vomiting, fever, and nuchal rigidity, and was diagnosed with disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system and concurrent active hepatitis B infection.
analysis_en.methods: The diagnostic process included cerebrospinal fluid analysis and chest computed tomography to confirm tuberculous meningitis and disseminated tuberculosis. Serology tests were used to identify active hepatitis B infection, and the treatment involved an intensified anti-tuberculosis regimen with adjustments for fetal safety.
analysis_en.main_results: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis confirmed tuberculous meningitis, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that early recognition and individualized treatment regimens, along with coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration, are essential for managing such complex cases. This case adds to the limited literature on the intersection of tuberculosis, hepatitis B, and pregnancy.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of multidisciplinary approaches in managing rare and complex infections in pregnant women, particularly in resource-limited settings where such comorbidities may be under-recognized.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a single case report, which limits its generalizability. However, the evidence is strong for the specific case presented, given the detailed clinical and diagnostic information provided.

title_zh: 妊娠晚期危重孕妇播散性结核病合并结核性脑膜炎和活动性乙型肝炎的多学科治疗:病例报告
source_body_en: Abstract Background Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) in pregnancy is rare but life-threatening, with substantial maternal and fetal risks. Third-trimester disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system with concurrent active hepatitis B infection has scarcely been reported, particularly among remote pastoral populations with limited healthcare access. This report highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of this triple comorbidity and underscores the value of multidisciplinary team (MDT) management in such complex scenarios. Case presentation A 24-year-old pastoralist at 30 weeks of gestation presented with headache, vomiting, fever, and nuchal rigidity. Cerebrospinal fluidanalysis confirmed TBM, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication. Given life-threatening intracranial hypertension [intracranial pressure (ICP) > 330 mmH 2 O] in late pregnancy, osmotic agents were withheld for fetal safety, and lumbar cisternal drainage was performed. An MDT comprising respiratory medicine, obstetrics, hepatology, pharmacy, and critical care nursing specialties was assembled. Anti-tuberculosis therapy was intensified to isoniazid, rifampicin, linezolid, and moxifloxacin; ethambutol was discontinued due to fetal optic neuritis, and tenofovir was added for hepatitis B management. Following stabilization, the patient was transferred to a higher-level facility at 35 weeks of gestation and underwent cesarean section at 36 weeks, delivering a live preterm female infant (2320 g, 1-min Apgar score of 8). Both mother and neonate were discharged without complications on December 1, 2025. Conclusions This case demonstrates that early recognition, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimens, and coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration are critical for achieving favorable outcomes in pregnant patients with disseminated tuberculosis complicated by TBM and concurrent hepatitis B infection. The successful management relied on integrated critical care and a multidisciplinary approach, which proved effective even in resource-limited pastoral settings.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 妊娠期结核性脑膜炎(TBM)很少见,但危及生命,对母体和胎儿具有很大的风险。妊娠晚期播散性结核病累及中枢神经系统并并发活动性乙型肝炎感染的报道很少,特别是在医疗保健机会有限的偏远牧区人群中。本报告强调了这种三重合并症的诊断和治疗挑战,并强调了多学科团队 (MDT) 管理在这种复杂情况下的价值。病例介绍 一名 24 岁牧民在妊娠 30 周时出现头痛、呕吐、发烧和颈项强直。脑脊液分析证实了 TBM,胸部计算机断层扫描显示弥漫性粟粒结节,提示血行播散性结核病。血清学乙型肝炎表面抗原、e抗原和核心抗体呈阳性,表明病毒复制活跃。由于妊娠晚期出现危及生命的颅内高压[颅内压(ICP)>330 mmH 2 O],为了胎儿安全,停用渗透剂,并进行腰大池引流。组建了包括呼吸内科、产科、肝病学、药学和重症监护护理专业的 MDT。抗结核治疗加强为异烟肼、利福平、利奈唑胺和莫西沙星;由于胎儿视神经炎而停用乙胺丁醇,并加用替诺福韦治疗乙型肝炎。病情稳定后,患者在妊娠 35 周时被转移到更高级别的机构,并在 36 周时接受剖腹产手术,产下一名活产早产女婴(2320 克,1 分钟阿普加评分为 8)。母亲和新生儿均于 2025 年 12 月 1 日出院,无并发症。结论 该病例表明,早期识别、个体化抗结核治疗方案和协调的多学科合作对于播散性结核病合并 TBM 并并发乙型肝炎感染的妊娠患者取得良好结局至关重要。成功的管理依赖于综合重症监护和多学科方法,即使在资源有限的牧区环境中,这种方法也被证明是有效的。

title: Knowledge, attitudes, practices, and vaccination gaps related to hepatitis B among adolescents in a hyperendemic, fragile setting: A cross-sectional study from Mogadishu, Somalia.
abstract: BackgroundHepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, yet evidence on adolescents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) toward HBV is limited in Somalia. This study assessed HBV-related KAP and associated factors among high school students in Mogadishu.ObjectivesTo assess HBV-related knowledge, attitudes, practices, and vaccination status among high school students in Mogadishu, Somalia, and identify associated factors.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 high school students using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics summarized KAP levels. Associations between sociodemographic variables and KAP outcomes were examined using chi-square tests and logistic regression.ResultsAlthough 98.0% of students had heard of HBV, 63.0% of participants demonstrated good knowledge of hepatitis B, while 37.0% had poor knowledge. Positive attitudes toward HBV were reported by 27.0% of participants, whereas 73.0% had negative attitudes. Just over half of respondents (52.5%) reported good preventive practices, while 47.5% had poor practices. HBV vaccination coverage was 39.3%. In multivariable analysis, grade level was significantly associated with the KAP domains, although the pattern of association varied across knowledge, attitudes, and practices.ConclusionHigh school students in Mogadishu exhibited substantial gaps in HBV knowledge, negative attitudes, and low vaccination uptake. Educational grade level was a key determinant of HBV-related KAP, highlighting the need for targeted, school-based interventions to strengthen adolescent HBV prevention.
journal: The International journal of risk & safety in medicine

title: Hepatite B crônica: progressão da doença, complicações e estratégias terapêuticas — uma revisão narrativa da literatura Chronic Hepatitis B: disease progression, complications, and therapeutic strategies — a literature review
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B is an important public health problem due to its potential to progress to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Disease progression is influenced by viral, immunological, clínical, metabolic, and host-related factors, as well as by conditions associated with diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up. This study aimed to analyze the available evidence on the clinical progression of chronic hepatitis B, its main associated factors, complications, and therapeutic strategies. This is a narrative literature review based on searches conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, LILACS, and SciELO, considering publications from January 2015 to July 2026 in Portuguese, English, and Spanish. Scientific studies, clinical guidelines, and technical and normative documents addressing the natural history of infection, factors associated with disease progression, complications, and treatment were prioritized. The literature indicates that the progression of chronic hepatitis B results from the interaction between viral replication, immune response, and host characteristics, and may also be influenced by coinfections, alcohol consumption, metabolic disorders, and conditions affecting access to healthcare. Antiviral therapy plays a central role in suppressing viral replication and reducing the risk of disease progression, whereas longitudinal follow-up remains essential for identifying complications and stratifying risk. In conclusion, the management of chronic hepatitis B requires an integrated approach involving prevention, early diagnosis, individualized assessment, timely treatment, and continuous follow-up.

title: Triple burden at the HIV–hepatitis B–malaria interface: viral–parasite interactions, epidemiological complexity and the case for integrated surveillance and community-based prevention in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and malaria overlap across sub-Saharan Africa, yet they differ in how they spread, how long they last and how programmes measure success. This critical narrative review examines the evidence for biological interaction at each interface, the diagnostic and epidemiological traps that their overlap creates, and the case for integrated surveillance and community prevention. HIV-associated immunosuppression consistently increases the frequency and severity of malaria, and acute malaria transiently raises plasma HIV RNA. HIV accelerates the natural history of chronic HBV. Because HIV treatment and prevention are shifting towards regimens and long-acting products with no activity against HBV, a documented hepatitis B surface antigen result has become essential before any regimen change. Antiretroviral and antimalarial drugs also interact in clinically relevant ways. A direct interaction between HBV and Plasmodium is plausible, through interferon-mediated suppression of HBV during malaria, but it rests mainly on animal models and small, inconsistent human studies, and no reliable estimate of triple infection exists. Fever, anaemia and abnormal liver tests during malaria can mask a concurrent chronic viral infection, and routine facility data can produce apparent coinfection patterns that reflect testing intensity rather than biology. Drawing on the World Health Organization’s guidance on integrated disease surveillance and response, we describe a detect–verify–act approach that links community signals, confirmatory testing and confidential longitudinal records, while each infection keeps its own indicators and review cycle. Integration should rest on shared delivery, not on assumed shared pathogenesis, and prospective cohorts and implementation trials are needed to show whether it improves outcomes and equity.

abstract_zh: 人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV)、乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和疟疾在撒哈拉以南非洲地区有重叠,但它们的传播方式、持续时间以及项目衡量成功的方式有所不同。这篇批判性的叙述性评论审查了每个界面的生物相互作用的证据、它们的重叠造成的诊断和流行病学陷阱,以及综合 监测 和社区预防的案例。HIV 相关的免疫抑制持续增加疟疾的发生频率和严重程度,而急性疟疾会暂时升高血浆 HIV RNA。HIV 加速了慢性 HBV 的自然病程。由于 HIV 治疗 和预防正在转向治疗方案和对 HBV 无活性的长效产品,因此在任何治疗方案改变之前,记录乙型肝炎表面抗原结果变得至关重要。抗逆转录病毒药物和抗疟药物也以临床相关方式相互作用。乙肝病毒和疟原虫之间的直接相互作用是合理的,通过疟疾期间干扰素介导的乙肝病毒抑制,但这种相互作用主要依赖于动物模型和小型、不一致的人体研究,并且不存在对三重感染的可靠估计。疟疾期间的发烧、贫血和肝脏检查异常可能会掩盖并发的慢性​​病毒感染,而常规设施数据可能会产生明显的合并感染模式,这些模式反映的是检测强度而不是生物学。借鉴世界卫生组织关于综合疾病 监测 和应对的指导,我们描述了一种检测-验证-行动方法,该方法将社区信号、确认性测试和机密纵向记录联系起来,同时每种感染都有自己的指标和审查周期。整合应该基于共享交付,而不是假设的共享 发病机制,并且需要前瞻性的 队列研究 和实施试验来证明它是否可以改善结果和公平性。

title: Disruption of the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry
abstract: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP–EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV–NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras–MAPK and PI3K–Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP–receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanism of hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) entry into hepatocytes, focusing on the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex. The researchers developed an in vitro assay to evaluate this interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupts the complex, selectively inhibiting HBV and HDV infection without affecting NTCP or EGFR physiological functions. Further analysis revealed that Oxy283, a derivative of Oxy229, has enhanced anti-HBV potency by targeting both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization. These findings highlight the NTCP–receptor complex as a potential antiviral target. The study's evidence is strong, as it is based on direct mechanistic analysis and selective inhibition of viral entry. However, the findings are limited to in vitro settings and do not include clinical or in vivo data.

title_zh: 破坏 NTCP-EGFR 受体复合物作为选择性抑制乙型和丁型肝炎病毒进入的策略
source_body_en: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP–EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV–NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras–MAPK and PI3K–Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP–receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

title: Nucleos(t)ide analogue discontinuation strategy to achieve the functional cure for chronic hepatitis B? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Functional cure rate is low during continuous nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy, and therapy suspension has demonstrated interesting off-treatment responses. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate how stable, HBsAg positive-virally suppressed patients would respond to drug discontinuation in terms of HBsAg clearance, clinical remission, virological relapses, alanine-aminotransferases (ALT) flares, and necessity of therapy reintroduction were performed. Included studies were prospective, experimental and observational studies, including data on outcomes after NA discontinuation in HBV DNA negative patients with positive HBsAg, involving at least 20 patients receiving entecavir or tenofovir, published from 2008 to February 2026, written in English language. RESULTS: A total of 28 papers (4495 patients) were included in the analysis, with low risk of bias: HBsAg clearance rate at 24, 48 and 96 weeks were of 3%, 8% and 11% (95% IC 1-8%, 4-15%, 7-15%) respectively, with low to moderate heterogeneity (I2=58.4%%, 66.5%, 47.3%); according to the HBeAg status at NA introduction, in those HBeAg negative the HBsAg clearance rates were 3%, 8% and 10% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively, while in those HBeAg positive 2.3 and 3.4% at 24 and 48 weeks, respectively. Overall a higher HBsAg clearance rate (39% at 96 weeks, 95% CI=10-78%, I2=83.3%) was described in patients with HBsAg <100 UI/ml at discontinuation. Treatment reintroduction due to virological and clinical relapse rates were 21%, 12%, and 17% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: These results showed an overall low rate of HBsAg clearance after NA discontinuation, except for the patients with low HBsAg titers at this time. Thus, NA discontinuation must be balanced in the single case for the risk of virological and clinical relapses.

source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Functional cure rate is low during continuous nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy, and therapy suspension has demonstrated interesting off-treatment responses. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate how stable, HBsAg positive-virally suppressed patients would respond to drug discontinuation in terms of HBsAg clearance, clinical remission, virological relapses, alanine-aminotransferases (ALT) flares, and necessity of therapy reintroduction were performed. Included studies were prospective, experimental and observational studies, including data on outcomes after NA discontinuation in HBV DNA negative patients with positive HBsAg, involving at least 20 patients receiving entecavir or tenofovir, published from 2008 to February 2026, written in English language. RESULTS: A total of 28 papers (4495 patients) were included in the analysis, with low risk of bias: HBsAg clearance rate at 24, 48 and 96 weeks were of 3%, 8% and 11% (95% IC 1-8%, 4-15%, 7-15%) respectively, with low to moderate heterogeneity (I2=58.4%%, 66.5%, 47.3%); according to the HBeAg status at NA introduction, in those HBeAg negative the HBsAg clearance rates were 3%, 8% and 10% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively, while in those HBeAg positive 2.3 and 3.4% at 24 and 48 weeks, respectively. Overall a higher HBsAg clearance rate (39% at 96 weeks, 95% CI=10-78%, I2=83.3%) was described in patients with HBsAg <100 UI/ml at discontinuation. Treatment reintroduction due to virological and clinical relapse rates were 21%, 12%, and 17% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: These results showed an overall low rate of HBsAg clearance after NA discontinuation, except for the patients with low HBsAg titers at this time. Thus, NA discontinuation must be balanced in the single case for the risk of virological and clinical relapses.

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决目前缺乏可靠方法预测慢性乙型肝炎患者对治疗反应的问题,因为长期抗病毒治疗可以逆转肝纤维化,但并非所有患者都能实现逆转。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本观点综述讨论了机器学习在改善慢性乙型肝炎患者纤维化逆转预测方面的潜力,重点关注临床工具在捕捉动态纤维化过程方面的局限性。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者回顾了机器学习如何应用于分析影像数据、整合临床和病理数据,并通过在抗病毒治疗期间进行连续测量来预测患者对治疗的反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 机器学习在三个领域已显示出早期但有希望的结果:定量影像分析、临床和病理数据的多模态整合,以及基于连续测量的动态预测患者对治疗的反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释认为,机器学习的最大价值在于补充现有工具,特别是在识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面,而不是取代它们。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,机器学习可能有助于提高慢性乙型肝炎治疗的功能性治愈率,并优化个性化治疗策略,从而改善纤维化逆转的预测能力并指导临床决策。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 目前的证据受到限制,因为大多数现有模型都是基于小规模、单一中心的回顾性数据,这可能影响其普适性,需要前瞻性多中心验证。

title: Fusion of segmental right-lobe IVIM-DWI metrics and GPR for non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B–related hepatic fibrosis: a pilot study
abstract: PURPOSE: A segmental intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging (IVIM-DWI)/gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase-to-platelet ratio (GPR) fusion model was evaluated for the non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) fibrosis (controls vs. advanced) and compared with the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4). METHODS: This retrospective study included 139 participants: 42 healthy controls (HCs), 46 with early hepatic fibrosis (EHF), and 51 with advanced hepatic fibrosis (AHF). IVIM-DWI parameters (apparent diffusion coefficient, slow diffusion component, fast diffusion component, and perfusion fraction) were extracted from segmental analysis of the right hepatic lobe (segments V-VIII). The GPR, APRI, and FIB-4 were calculated from laboratory values. The IVIM + GPR fusion model was developed using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap internal validation. RESULTS: For HCs vs. EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). The IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.745, 95% CI: 0.643-0.847) outperformed IVIM alone (AUC = 0.652) and GPR alone (AUC = 0.730) but did not outperform APRI or FIB-4. AHF, the IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.698) was comparable to APRI (0.573) and FIB-4 (0.637), with no significant differences among methods. CONCLUSION: FIB-4/APRI outperformed the fusion model for controls vs. early fibrosis, whereas fusion added no value over GPR for early vs. In the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, HCs vs. EHF discriminates between HCs and established fibrosis rather than detecting incident fibrosis. The model should be considered, at most, a supplementary, opportunistic adjunct during abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rather than a replacement for FIB-4/APRI. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The GPR uses only gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase and platelets, making it practical in resource- limited settings. The fusion model may provide supplementary, opportunistic information during abdominal MRI or when serum markers are confounded by extrahepatic factors, but it should remain complementary pending validation in larger cohorts; FIB-4 and APRI remain first-line where laboratory panels are available.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究包括 139 名参与者:42 名健康对照 (HC)、46 名早期肝纤维化 (EHF) 和 51 名晚期肝纤维化 (AHF)。
elements_zh.methods: IVIM-DWI 参数(表观扩散系数、慢扩散成分、快扩散成分和灌注分数)是从右肝叶(段 V-VIII)的分段分析中提取的。GPR、APRI 和 FIB-4 是根据实验室值计算的。IVIM + GPR 融合模型是使用逻辑回归开发的。使用接收器操作特征分析和引导程序内部验证来评估模型性能。
elements_zh.main_results: EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). For AHF, the IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.698) was comparable to APRI (0.573) and FIB-4 (0.637), with no significant differences among methods.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: IVIM + GPR 融合模型可以在腹部 MRI 期间或当血清标志物被肝外因素混淆时提供补充的机会性信息,但它应该保持互补,等待在更大的 队列研究 中进行验证。

analysis_en.methods: IVIM-DWI parameters (apparent diffusion coefficient, slow diffusion component, fast diffusion component, and perfusion fraction) were extracted from segmental analysis of the right hepatic lobe (segments V-VIII). The GPR, APRI, and FIB-4 were calculated from laboratory values. The IVIM + GPR fusion model was developed using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap internal validation.
analysis_en.main_results: EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The fusion model should be considered, at most, a supplementary, opportunistic adjunct during abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rather than a replacement for FIB-4/APRI. analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, HCs vs. EHF discriminates between HCs and established fibrosis rather than detecting incident fibrosis. title_zh: 分段右叶 IVIM-DWI 指标与 GPR 的融合,用于 慢性乙型肝炎 相关肝纤维化的无创评估:一项试点研究
source_body_en: PURPOSE: A segmental intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging (IVIM-DWI)/gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase-to-platelet ratio (GPR) fusion model was evaluated for the non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) fibrosis (controls vs. advanced) and compared with the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4). METHODS: This retrospective study included 139 participants: 42 healthy controls (HCs), 46 with early hepatic fibrosis (EHF), and 51 with advanced hepatic fibrosis (AHF). IVIM-DWI parameters (apparent diffusion coefficient, slow diffusion component, fast diffusion component, and perfusion fraction) were extracted from segmental analysis of the right hepatic lobe (segments V-VIII). The GPR, APRI, and FIB-4 were calculated from laboratory values. The IVIM + GPR fusion model was developed using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap internal validation. RESULTS: For HCs vs. EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). The IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.745, 95% CI: 0.643-0.847) outperformed IVIM alone (AUC = 0.652) and GPR alone (AUC = 0.730) but did not outperform APRI or FIB-4. AHF, the IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.698) was comparable to APRI (0.573) and FIB-4 (0.637), with no significant differences among methods. CONCLUSION: FIB-4/APRI outperformed the fusion model for controls vs. early fibrosis, whereas fusion added no value over GPR for early vs. In the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, HCs vs. EHF discriminates between HCs and established fibrosis rather than detecting incident fibrosis. The model should be considered, at most, a supplementary, opportunistic adjunct during abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rather than a replacement for FIB-4/APRI. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The GPR uses only gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase and platelets, making it practical in resource- limited settings. The fusion model may provide supplementary, opportunistic information during abdominal MRI or when serum markers are confounded by extrahepatic factors, but it should remain complementary pending validation in larger cohorts; FIB-4 and APRI remain first-line where laboratory panels are available.

title: Evaluation of point-of-care testing (POCT) for blood-borne infections in forensic autopsy specimens.
abstract: ABSTRACT Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection enables rapid screening for blood-borne viral infections and may be particularly valuable in forensic autopsy settings, where incomplete antemortem medical histories and invasive procedures increase the risk of occupational exposure. However, its performance in postmortem specimens remains unclear. We evaluated the applicability of LFIA-based POCT for detecting human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis B virus (HBV) in autopsy specimens, focusing on postmortem decomposition and the use of solid organ tissues as alternatives to blood. A total of 309 cases were analyzed using LFIA and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) across blood, liver, and spleen specimens. Agreement was assessed using overall, positive, and negative percent agreement and Cohen’s kappa coefficient ( κ ). Positivity rates were compared by specimen type and decomposition status. LFIA agreement with qPCR varied by marker and specimen type, with substantial agreement for HIV and HCV antibody detection in blood and lower agreement in liver and spleen. Fresh specimens generally demonstrated higher LFIA positivity rates than decomposed specimens. Among specimens meeting predefined qPCR positivity criteria, LFIA-positive specimens tended to exhibit higher viral loads than LFIA-negative specimens, reaching statistical significance for HBV in liver, with similar but non-significant trends for blood HBV and liver HCV. LFIA-based POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in postmortem settings, particularly when blood is available. Nevertheless, negative results do not exclude infection—especially with low viral loads or advanced decomposition—and should be confirmed by molecular testing. IMPORTANCE Forensic personnel performing autopsies face significant occupational risks from exposure to blood-borne viruses, including human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, and hepatitis C virus. Unlike clinical settings, forensic autopsies frequently involve bodies with unknown infection histories, making rapid infection screening essential for personnel safety. Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection offers a rapid, infrastructure-free screening option; however, its performance in postmortem specimens has not been systematically evaluated. This study suggests that rapid immunochromatographic POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in forensic autopsy settings, particularly when blood specimens are available. However, a negative result does not exclude infection, especially in cases with low viral load or advanced decomposition, and confirmatory molecular testing remains necessary. These findings provide practical guidance for forensic professionals on appropriate specimen selection and interpretation of LFIA results, ultimately supporting safer autopsy practices.

abstract_zh: 摘要 基于侧流免疫分析 (LFIA) 的病毒抗原和抗体检测即时检测 (POCT) 能够快速筛查血源性病毒感染,在法医尸检环境中可能特别有价值,因为在法医尸检环境中,不完整的生前病史和侵入性操作会增加职业暴露的风险。然而,其在尸检标本中的表现仍不清楚。我们评估了基于 LFIA 的 POCT 在检测尸检标本中人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV)、丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 和 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 方面的适用性,重点关注死后分解和使用实体器官组织作为血液替代品。使用 LFIA 和定量聚合酶链反应 (qPCR) 对血液、肝脏和脾脏标本总共 309 例进行了分析。使用总体一致性百分比、正一致性百分比和负一致性百分比以及 Cohen 的 kappa 系数 (κ) 来评估一致性。根据标本类型和分解状态比较阳性率。LFIA 与 qPCR 的一致性因标记物和样本类型而异,血液中 HIV 和 HCV 抗体检测的一致性较高,而肝脏和脾脏的一致性较低。新鲜标本的 LFIA 阳性率通常高于腐烂标本。在符合预定 qPCR 阳性标准的标本中,LFIA 阳性标本往往比 LFIA 阴性标本表现出更高的病毒载量,肝脏中 HBV 达到统计学显着性,血液 HBV 和肝脏 HCV 具有相似但不显着的趋势。基于 LFIA 的 POCT 可以作为尸检中的初步筛查工具,特别是在有血液的情况下。然而,阴性结果并不能排除感染,尤其是病毒载量较低或分解较严重的情况,应通过分子检测来确认。重要性 进行尸检的法医人员面临着暴露于血源性病毒(包括人类免疫缺陷病毒、乙型肝炎病毒 和丙型肝炎病毒)的重大职业风险。与临床环境不同,法医尸检经常涉及感染史未知的尸体,因此快速感染筛查对于人员安全至关重要。基于侧流免疫分析 (LFIA) 的病毒抗原和抗体检测即时检测 (POCT) 提供了一种快速、无需基础设施的筛查选项;然而,其在尸检标本中的性能尚未得到系统评估。这项研究表明,快速免疫层析 POCT 可以作为法医尸检环境中的初步筛查工具,特别是在有血液样本的情况下。然而,阴性结果并不能排除感染,特别是在病毒载量低或分解严重的情况下,仍然需要进行确认性分子检测。这些发现为法医专业人员适当选择标本和解释 LFIA 结果提供了实用指导,最终支持更安全的尸检实践。

title: Evaluation of Anti-HBs Levels in Children Who Received Three Doses of Hepatitis B Vaccine According to Age Groups and Gestational Age: A Retrospective Single-Center Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background Anti-HBs levels decline after infant hepatitis B vaccination, especially during school age and adolescence, but data evaluating both age and gestational age-related effects in a large pediatric cohort remain limited. Methods In this retrospective, single-center, cross-sectional study, we included 6,510 children aged 9 months–18 years who had completed three hepatitis B vaccine doses and had at least one quantitative anti-HBs measurement between 2021 and 2023. Seronegativity was defined as anti-HBs < 10 mIU/mL. Children were grouped by age (9 months–5 years, 6–11 years, 12–18 years) and gestational age (early preterm < 32 weeks, late preterm 32–36+6 weeks, term ≥ 37 weeks). Comparisons used Kruskal–Wallis, chi-square, ANCOVA, and logistic regression. Results Overall seronegativity was 30.6% (1,989/6,510), and the median anti-HBs level was 34.30 mIU/mL (IQR 6.72–143.23). Anti-HBs levels decreased significantly with age (medians 99.17, 23.94, and 12.55 mIU/mL for the 9 months–5 years, 6–11 years, and 12–18 years groups; p < 0.001), while seronegativity increased (14.4%, 33.9%, and 45.5%; p < 0.001). Age group was the strongest independent predictor of seronegativity (6–11 years: OR 3.218, 95% CI 2.521–4.108; 12–18 years: OR 5.348, 95% CI 4.183–6.839). Among 4,242 children with gestational age data, gestational age was not independently associated with seronegativity after adjustment (p = 0.109), and seronegativity rates were comparable across groups (34.5% early preterm, 25.8% late preterm, 36.9% term; p = 0.168). In children born at term, mean anti-HBs was 525.05 ± 401.31 mIU/mL at ≤ 3 years versus 74.99 ± 143.60 mIU/mL at ≥ 4 years. Conclusion Anti-HBs levels decline significantly with age after three-dose hepatitis B vaccination, whereas gestational age is not an independent predictor of seronegativity. Targeted serological follow-up and individualized booster strategies, particularly for high-risk groups, may be warranted.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate how anti-HBs levels change with age and gestational age in children who received three doses of hepatitis B vaccine, as data on these factors in a large pediatric cohort are limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted involving 6,510 children aged 9 months to 18 years who had completed three hepatitis B vaccine doses and had at least one quantitative anti-HBs measurement between 2021 and 2023.
analysis.methods: The study used statistical methods including Kruskal–Wallis, chi-square, ANCOVA, and logistic regression to compare anti-HBs levels and seronegativity across age groups and gestational age categories.
analysis.main_results: Overall seronegativity was 30.6% (1,989/6,510), and the median anti-HBs level was 34.30 mIU/mL (IQR 6.72–143.23). Anti-HBs levels decreased significantly with age, while seronegativity increased across age groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that anti-HBs levels decline significantly with age after three-dose hepatitis B vaccination, and gestational age was not found to be an independent predictor of seronegativity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted serological follow-up and individualized booster strategies may be necessary, particularly for high-risk groups, to maintain adequate immunity against hepatitis B.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and single-center setting, which may affect generalizability. However, the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and statistical adjustments.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated anti-HBs levels in children who received three doses of hepatitis B vaccine, focusing on age and gestational age effects. It found that seronegativity increased significantly with age, while gestational age was not independently associated with seronegativity. The results highlight the need for targeted serological follow-up and individualized booster strategies, especially for high-risk groups. The study's retrospective, single-center design may limit generalizability, but the large sample size and statistical methods support its findings. These results contribute to understanding the long-term immune response to hepatitis B vaccination in children and may inform future vaccination strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估接受三剂乙型肝炎 疫苗 的儿童的抗 HBs 水平如何随年龄和胎龄变化,因为大型儿科 疫苗 中这些因素的数据有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性、单中心、横断面研究涉及 6,510 名 9 个月至 18 岁的儿童,他们在 2021 年至 2023 年间完成了三剂乙型肝炎 疫苗 剂量,并至少进行了一次定量抗 HBs 测量。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用了 Kruskal-Wallis、卡方、ANCOVA 和逻辑回归等统计方法来比较不同年龄组和胎龄类别的抗 HBs 水平和血清阴性。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体血清阴性率为 30.6% (1,989/6,510),中位抗 HBs 水平为 34.30 mIU/mL (IQR 6.72–143.23)。抗 HBs 水平随着年龄的增长而显着下降,而血清阴性水平则随着年龄组的增加而增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,在接受三剂乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 后,抗 HBs 水平随着年龄的增长而显着下降,并且未发现孕龄是血清阴性的独立预测因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有针对性的血清学随访和个体化加强策略可能是必要的,特别是对于高危人群,以保持足够的乙型肝炎免疫力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和单中心设置而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。然而,由于样本量大和统计调整,证据是强有力的。

title: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy
abstract: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people. The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs. In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes. This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care. This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒和乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒检测:意大利当前状况与展望
source_body_en: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people. The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs. In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes. This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care. This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

title: Anti-Viral Treatment Eligibility and Treatment Uptake Among People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Australia: The REACH-B Study.
abstract: Treatment indication for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) varies across clinical guidelines. This study evaluated treatment eligibility and uptake in a large Australian cohort of people with CHB. The REACH-B study recruited people with CHB managed through a national network of healthcare services. Participants were categorised into three groups: (1) receiving antiviral therapy; (2) untreated despite eligibility; (3) untreated and ineligible. Treatment eligibility was determined using Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) criteria, and by international clinical guidelines. Among 3648 participants (56% male; median age 48 years; 49% born in North-East or South-East Asia; 27% First Nations Australians), 14% were HBeAg positive and 7% had cirrhosis. Overall, 47% (n = 1666) were on antiviral therapy, 45% (n = 1573) were untreated and ineligible and 7% (n = 251) were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria. In adjusted analysis, the likelihood of remaining untreated despite eligibility was higher among women (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34, 1.88) and younger participants (age 41-60 vs. > 60 years: aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.01-2.28; ≤ 40 vs. > 60 years: aOR 2.65, 95% CI 1.60, 4.40). The proportion untreated despite eligibility increased to 13% when applying 2024 World Health Organisation guidelines and ranged 2%-44% based on other guidelines, highlighting the variability across the guidelines. In conclusion, among REACH-B participants, most eligible individuals receive treatment. Lower treatment uptake among women and younger people despite eligibility partly reflects lower threshold for elevated ALT in women, and clinician determination of non-CHB related ALT elevation. As treatment guidelines evolve and eligibility criteria broaden, monitoring treatment patterns is important.

analysis_en.methods: Treatment eligibility was determined using Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) criteria, and by international clinical guidelines.
analysis_en.main_results: Overall, 47% (n = 1666) were on antiviral therapy, 45% (n = 1573) were untreated and ineligible and 7% (n = 251) were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: In adjusted analysis, the likelihood of remaining untreated despite eligibility was higher among women (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34, 1.88) and younger participants (age 41-60 vs. > 60 years: aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.01-2.28; ≤ 40 vs. 41-60 years: aOR 1.85, 95% CI 1.34-2.56). title_zh: 澳大利亚 治疗 患者的抗病毒 治疗 资格和 治疗 的使用情况:REACH-B 研究。
source_body_en: Treatment indication for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) varies across clinical guidelines. This study evaluated treatment eligibility and uptake in a large Australian cohort of people with CHB. The REACH-B study recruited people with CHB managed through a national network of healthcare services. Participants were categorised into three groups: (1) receiving antiviral therapy; (2) untreated despite eligibility; (3) untreated and ineligible. Treatment eligibility was determined using Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) criteria, and by international clinical guidelines. Among 3648 participants (56% male; median age 48 years; 49% born in North-East or South-East Asia; 27% First Nations Australians), 14% were HBeAg positive and 7% had cirrhosis. Overall, 47% (n = 1666) were on antiviral therapy, 45% (n = 1573) were untreated and ineligible and 7% (n = 251) were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria. In adjusted analysis, the likelihood of remaining untreated despite eligibility was higher among women (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34, 1.88) and younger participants (age 41-60 vs. > 60 years: aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.01-2.28; ≤ 40 vs. > 60 years: aOR 2.65, 95% CI 1.60, 4.40). The proportion untreated despite eligibility increased to 13% when applying 2024 World Health Organisation guidelines and ranged 2%-44% based on other guidelines, highlighting the variability across the guidelines. In conclusion, among REACH-B participants, most eligible individuals receive treatment. Lower treatment uptake among women and younger people despite eligibility partly reflects lower threshold for elevated ALT in women, and clinician determination of non-CHB related ALT elevation. As treatment guidelines evolve and eligibility criteria broaden, monitoring treatment patterns is important.

title: Selection, escape and the limits of inference in Middle Eastern hepatitis B virus genotype D: an analysis of 824 curated public sequences
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus genotype D (HBV/D) predominates across the Middle East, yet questions asked of its public sequence archive are rarely preceded by a test of whether that archive can answer them. Methods HBV records of 500–4,000 nt from fifteen Middle Eastern countries were retrieved from GenBank, genotype assigned against a 98-genome A–H reference panel, and records filtered on collection date, surface-gene coverage, ambiguity and within-country identity. Curated sequences were projected onto a genotype D reference (LC519816.1), giving a reference-anchored matrix across the surface and reverse-transcriptase frames. A maximum-likelihood tree was inferred under GTR+Γ, temporal signal tested by root-to-tip regression, and ancestral country states reconstructed under a discrete migration model and re-estimated on five country-balanced subsamples. Results Of 4,398 records retrieved, 824 sequences from ten countries passed curation (Iraq, 94). Canonical resistance substitutions (rtL180M, rtM204V/I, rtV173L) and surface escape substitutions (sP120S/T, sS143L, sD144A/E/G, sG145R/A) were recovered, with rtL180M and rtM204V/I most frequent (each >2%) the compensatory and escape substitutions each below 2%, as in clinical series of treated genotype D infection. Twelve codons showed diversifying selection by two methods, only one inside a determinant and none at classical escape positions; antigenic-loop selection did not differ from the rest of the protein (Mann-Whitney p = 0.50; permutation p = 0.61). Four planned analyses failed: root-to-tip regression gave R2 = 0.002, so the dataset cannot be dated; the apparent Iranian source signal (+200 net exports) fell to +1.2 under balanced subsampling, where Syria (+27.0) displaced Iran; median pairwise distance was 0.0128 substitutions/site, with 97.0% of sequences in one component at 0.015; and subgenotype assignment left only 7.2% of sequences resolvable at a 0.005 margin. Conclusions Substantively, the HBsAg antigenic loop shows no excess of diversifying selection despite immune surveillance, and monitored escape positions carry no site-level signature, consistent with escape arising as rare individually selected events rather than a selective regime. Methodologically, the archive supports mutational and selection epidemiology but not dating, source attribution, transmission clustering or subgenotype assignment from surface-gene data; the constraint is sequence length and sampling design, not sample size.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the public sequence archive of hepatitis B virus genotype D to determine if it could support inferences about selection and escape mechanisms in the Middle East. The background highlighted that HBV/D is prevalent in the region, but its sequence archive has not been rigorously tested for its ability to answer specific questions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 824 curated public sequences from ten Middle Eastern countries, including Iraq, to explore patterns of diversifying selection and escape substitutions. These sequences were sourced from GenBank and filtered based on collection date, surface-gene coverage, ambiguity, and within-country identity.
analysis.methods: The sequences were projected onto a genotype D reference, and a maximum-likelihood tree was inferred under GTR+Γ. Temporal signal was tested via root-to-tip regression, and ancestral country states were reconstructed using a discrete migration model, re-estimated on five country-balanced subsamples.
analysis.main_results: Of 4,398 retrieved records, 824 sequences from ten countries passed curation. Canonical resistance substitutions (rtL180M, rtM204V/I) and surface escape substitutions (sP120S/T, sS143L, sD144A/E/G, sG145R/A) were identified, with rtL180M and rtM204V/I being the most frequent (>2%). analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the HBsAg antigenic loop does not show an excess of diversifying selection, and escape positions lack site-level signatures, suggesting escape arises from rare individually selected events rather than a consistent selective regime. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the understanding of immune-driven evolution in HBV/D and highlight the limitations of using surface-gene data for source attribution or transmission clustering. abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 乙型肝炎病毒 基因型 D (HBV/D) 在整个中东地区占主导地位,但在对其公共序列档案提出问题之前很少先测试该档案是否能够回答这些问题。方法 从 GenBank 检索来自 15 个中东国家的 500-4,000 nt HBV 记录,根据 98-基因组 A-H 参考组分配基因型,并根据收集日期、表面基因覆盖度、模糊性和国内身份过滤记录。将策划的序列投影到基因型 D 参考 (LC519816.1) 上,从而在表面和反转录酶框架上提供参考锚定矩阵。在 GTR+Γ 下推断最大似然树,通过根到尖回归测试时间信号,在离散迁移模型下重建祖先国家,并在五个国家平衡子样本上重新估计。结果 在检索到的 4,398 条记录中,来自 10 个国家的 824 条序列通过了管理(伊拉克,94 条)。恢复了规范抗性替换(rtL180M、rtM204V/I、rtV173L)和表面逃逸替换(sP120S/T、sS143L、sD144A/E/G、sG145R/A),其中 rtL180M 和 rtM204V/I 最常见(每个 >2%),补偿和逃逸替换如下2%,如治疗 D 基因型感染的临床系列。十二个密码子通过两种方法表现出多样化选择,只有一个在决定簇内,没有一个在经典逃逸位置;抗原环选择与蛋白质的其余部分没有差异(Mann-Whitney p = 0.50;排列 p = 0.61)。四个计划分析失败:从根到尖回归得出 R2 = 0.002,因此无法确定数据集的日期;在平衡二次抽样下,明显的伊朗源信号(+200 净出口)降至+1.2,其中叙利亚(+27.0)取代了伊朗;中位成对距离为 0.0128 个取代/位点,其中一个组件中 97.0% 的序列为 0.015;亚基因型分配仅留下 7.2% 的序列可在 0.005 的裕度下解析。结论 实质上,尽管有免疫 监测,HBsAg 抗原环并未表现出过度的多样化选择,并且监测的逃逸位置不携带位点水平特征,这与逃逸作为罕见的单独选择事件而不是选择性机制一致。从方法上讲,该档案支持突变和选择 传播,但不支持约会、来源归因、传播 聚类或表面基因数据的亚基因型分配;约束是序列长度和抽样设计,而不是样本大小。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 乙型肝炎病毒 D 基因型的公共序列档案,以确定它是否可以支持有关中东选择和逃逸机制的推论。背景强调了 HBV/D 在该地区流行,但其序列档案尚未经过严格测试其回答特定问题的能力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了来自包括伊拉克在内的十个中东国家的 824 个精心策划的公共序列,以探索多样化选择和逃避替代的模式。这些序列源自 GenBank,并根据收集日期、表面基因覆盖度、模糊性和国内身份进行过滤。
analysis_zh.methods: 将序列投影到基因型 D 参考上,并在 GTR+Γ 下推断最大似然树。通过从根到尖的回归测试时间信号,并使用离散迁移模型重建祖先国家,并在五个国家平衡子样本上重新估计。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 4,398 个检索记录中,来自 10 个国家的 824 个序列通过了管理。确定了规范耐药替代(rtL180M、rtM204V/I)和表面逃逸替代(sP120S/T、sS143L、sD144A/E/G、sG145R/A),其中 rtL180M 和 rtM204V/I 最常见(>2%)。十二个密码子显示出多样化的选择,但没有一个位于经典的逃逸位置内。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,HBsAg 抗原环没有表现出过度的多样化选择,并且逃逸位置缺乏位点水平的特征,这表明逃逸源于罕见的单独选择事件,而不是一致的选择机制。这一发现是新颖的,因为它挑战了 HBV/D 中免疫驱动选择的假设。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现有助于理解 HBV/D 中免疫驱动的 进化,并强调使用表面基因数据进行来源归因或 传播 聚类的局限性。这对于改进 监测 和 D 基因型乙型肝炎的诊断策略具有重要意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 数据集缺乏时间信号并且无法确定日期,并且由于序列长度和采样设计,亚基因型分配受到限制。尽管存在这些局限性,但证据并不充分,因为该研究提供了对策划序列及其进化模式的详细分析。

title: Prevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis B core antibodies among pregnant women in Yemen
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B infection is a public health concern worldwide. It is associated with high rates of mother-tochild transmission, yet there are no published studies on the infection among pregnant women in the southern and eastern governorates of Yemen. Aim: To assess the prevalence of hepatitis B infection among pregnant women attending primary health care centres in Yemen. Methods: Between December 2023 and February 2024, we interviewed and tested 921 pregnant Yemeni women attending primary health care centres for antenatal care services in Aden, Mukalla and Marib governorates of Yemen. We analysed the data using SPSS version 25 and used chi-square to test the association between the categorical variables. P = 0.05 was taken as statistical significance. Results: Forty-five of the 921 pregnant women (5%) were reactive for HBsAg (95% CI; 3.6–6.5%) and 66 (7.2%) for (95% CI; 5.6%-9%). Marib Governorate had the highest prevalence of HBsAg (10.4%) and anti-HBc (12.7%). Type of governorate and social status of the women were significantly associated with HBsAg and anti-HBc reactivity. First trimester was associated with HBsAg. Conclusion: The moderate prevalence of hepatitis B among pregnant women in Yemen increases the risk of motherto-child transmission and a high-risk of chronic hepatitis in infected children. It indicates the need for preventive interventions, including routine screening of pregnant women and introduction of birth dose hepatitis B vaccine.

title: Community-Based Detection of Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and Herpes Simplex Viruses in Northern Thailand
abstract: Blood-borne viral infections remain important public health concerns worldwide. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) are well-established transfusion-transmissible pathogens, whereas the epidemiological significance of detecting herpes simplex virus (HSV) DNA in peripheral blood remains unclear. This cross-sectional study investigated HBsAg, anti-HCV antibodies, and HSV-1/HSV-2 DNA in a community-based population in northern Thailand. Serum samples from 779 participants were tested for HBsAg and anti-HCV using rapid immunochromatographic assays, while whole-blood samples from 639 participants were tested for HSV-1 and HSV-2 DNA using real-time PCR. HBsAg and anti-HCV were detected in 3.0% (23/779) and 1.8% (14/779) of participants, respectively. HSV-1 and HSV-2 DNA were each detected in 0.5% (3/639) of whole-blood samples. In the regression analysis, higher body weight was associated with lower odds of HBsAg detection (AOR = 0.955, 95% CI: 0.929–0.982; p = 0.001). These findings provide updated community-based epidemiological data on HBV, HCV, and HSV in northern Thailand. Because HSV DNA was detected infrequently and sequence confirmation was limited, the HSV findings should be interpreted with caution. Further studies involving larger populations, quantitative viral-load measurements, and longitudinal sampling are needed.

title: Serum platelet-derived growth factor-BB as a noninvasive biomarker of significant liver fibrosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major cause of progressive liver fibrosis (LF), cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Although noninvasive fibrosis assessment is essential, current tools have practical and diagnostic limitations. Platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)—a profibrogenic mediator of hepatic stellate cell activation—may be a biologically relevant fibrosis biomarker. This study examined the ability of serum PDGF-BB to detect significant fibrosis in CHB patients which is defined as liver stiffness > 7 kPa by vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE; FibroScan). Methods This cross-sectional exploratory diagnostic accuracy study included 90 treatment-naive adults with CHB attending Tanta University Hospitals and Kafr El-Sheikh University Hospitals. All participants underwent clinical evaluation; routine laboratory testing, including HBsAg, HBeAg, and serum HBV DNA; abdominal ultrasonography; serum PDGF-BB measurement by ELISA; and FibroScan examination. VCTE-defined significant fibrosis (F2–F4) was set as liver stiffness > 7 kPa. A non-randomized convenience sampling approach was used to enroll participants, and the optimal PDGF-BB cutoff was established based on the ROC curve derived from this cohort. Results Among 90 patients, 69 (76.7%) had F0-F1 fibrosis and 21 (23.3%) had F2-F4 fibrosis. HBeAg was positive in 21.1% of patients and median HBV DNA was 4.47 (3.68–5.31) log10 IU/mL Median serum PDGF-BB was significantly increased in patients with F2-F4 than in those with F0-F1 fibrosis: 2500.8 (2028.25-2721.8) vs. 777.13 (479.21-1743.15) pg/mL, respectively ( p < 0.001). Serum PDGF-BB discriminated VCTE-defined significant fibrosis at an exploratory, internally derived cutoff of ≥ 1885.9 pg/mL, with an AUC of 0.905 (95% CI 0.816–0.994), sensitivity of 85.7%, specificity of 84.1%, positive predictive value of 62.1%, negative predictive value of 95.1% (at the 23.3% prevalence of this cohort), and overall accuracy of 84.4% (Youden index 0.698; p < 0.001). PDGF-BB had a numerically higher AUC than APRI (0.717) and GPR (0.715), but these differences did not reach statistical significance after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. It did not differ significantly from FIB-4 (0.780) and did not outperform platelet count (0.980) or INR (0.931). Conclusions Serum PDGF-BB demonstrated good discrimination for VCTE-defined significant fibrosis in treatment-naive patients with CHB. Its negative predictive value of 95%, though prevalence-dependent, suggests potential utility as a triage or adjunctive biomarker. However, these findings are preliminary and require external validation before clinical implementation or substitution for elastography.
