title: Pooled prevalence of infectious diseases among first responders in the prehospital setting: A systematic review with meta-analysis by occupation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers. METHODS: Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool. RESULTS: Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p = 0.039. CONCLUSIONS: Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

title: Challenges and Improvement Strategies to Increase Staff Vaccination Coverage in Long-Term Care.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Keeping staff in post-acute and long-term care (PALTC) settings up to date on adult vaccinations is important to protect them and reduce the spread of vaccine-preventable illness to residents. This quality improvement (QI) project aimed to increase vaccination coverage among PALTC staff while exploring improvement strategies tailored to this setting. DESIGN: QI project conducted in 2, 12-month cohorts between 2022 and 2024. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: QI teams from 15 skilled nursing facilities and 6 assisted living facilities across 9 states participated in the QI project. QI teams included staff and administrators working at the facility and corporate level in roles such as medical directors, directors/assistant directors of nursing, and infection preventionists. METHODS: QI teams implemented vaccination strategies, reported monthly staff vaccination coverage for 3 vaccines (COVID-19, influenza, and hepatitis B), received monthly technical assistance, and met quarterly with other facilities to share lessons learned. We report staff vaccination coverage at baseline and end point by vaccine, highlight common challenges across participating facilities, and provide examples of facilities' QI strategies. RESULTS: Most facilities did not improve staff vaccination coverage. Only 1 of 16 facilities with complete COVID-19 coverage data (6%) showed a modest improvement over time, 7 of 15 facilities with complete influenza coverage data (47%) maintained or improved coverage, and 4 of 6 facilities with complete hepatitis B coverage data (67%) showed improvement. Facilities focused their QI efforts on making vaccination convenient, respecting staff autonomy, and engaging staff in dialog but were challenged by staffing shortages, limited data infrastructure, and vaccine hesitancy. Facilities found it especially difficult to gather and report immunization data for staff; in some cases, low coverage reflected missing data. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Improving PALTC staff vaccination coverage nationally will require addressing data gaps, making vaccination convenient and affordable for staff, and addressing vaccine hesitancy through respectful dialog.

source_records.title: Challenges and Improvement Strategies to Increase Staff Vaccination Coverage in Long-Term Care.
source_records.abstract: Objectives Keeping staff in post-acute and long-term care (PALTC) settings up to date on adult vaccinations is important to protect them and reduce the spread of vaccine-preventable illness to residents. This quality improvement (QI) project aimed to increase vaccination coverage among PALTC staff while exploring improvement strategies tailored to this setting. Design QI project conducted in 2, 12-month cohorts between 2022 and 2024. Setting and participants QI teams from 15 skilled nursing facilities and 6 assisted living facilities across 9 states participated in the QI project. QI teams included staff and administrators working at the facility and corporate level in roles such as medical directors, directors/assistant directors of nursing, and infection preventionists. Methods QI teams implemented vaccination strategies, reported monthly staff vaccination coverage for 3 vaccines (COVID-19, influenza, and hepatitis B), received monthly technical assistance, and met quarterly with other facilities to share lessons learned. We report staff vaccination coverage at baseline and end point by vaccine, highlight common challenges across participating facilities, and provide examples of facilities' QI strategies. Results Most facilities did not improve staff vaccination coverage. Only 1 of 16 facilities with complete COVID-19 coverage data (6%) showed a modest improvement over time, 7 of 15 facilities with complete influenza coverage data (47%) maintained or improved coverage, and 4 of 6 facilities with complete hepatitis B coverage data (67%) showed improvement. Facilities focused their QI efforts on making vaccination convenient, respecting staff autonomy, and engaging staff in dialog but were challenged by staffing shortages, limited data infrastructure, and vaccine hesitancy. Facilities found it especially difficult to gather and report immunization data for staff; in some cases, low coverage reflected missing data. Conclusions and implications Improving PALTC staff vaccination coverage nationally will require addressing data gaps, making vaccination convenient and affordable for staff, and addressing vaccine hesitancy through respectful dialog.

title: Aflatoxin B1 exposure through peanuts worldwide: national level occurrence and exposure assessment.
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a mycotoxin, or fungal toxin, that contaminates maize, peanuts, and tree nuts grown in warm regions of the world. It causes liver cancer and is synergistic with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to multiplicatively increase cancer risk. Peanuts (also called groundnuts) are a major source of aflatoxin exposure in many populations worldwide. We conducted a systematic data review to examine the occurrence of AFB1 in peanut food products in 106 nations. We then conducted a dietary exposure assessment based on this occurrence dataset and consumption of peanuts in these nations, to compare trends across the time periods from 1990 to 2024. 22 nations experienced a substantial increase in aflatoxin exposure through peanut consumption, and 22 nations experienced a substantial decrease. Changes in exposure are largely driven by changes in intake levels. Many sub-Saharan African populations have alarmingly high levels of aflatoxin exposure, due to high contamination coupled with high consumption. Detection methods are shown to demonstrate recent improvements in sensitivity. These findings are important given the health risks of high aflatoxin exposure; most notably liver cancer.

title: Sex and Etiology Differences in Overall Survival and Adverse Liver Events in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: An International Multicenter Study.
abstract: Sex-associated differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) prognosis remain incompletely characterized across major etiologies. In this retrospective international multicenter cohort study, we included 7623 consecutive patients with newly diagnosed HCC from 41 centers in five countries and evaluated the associations of sex and four-level etiology with overall survival (OS) and the first adverse liver event (hepatic decompensation, liver failure, or liver-related death). Sex-related OS was evaluated in the full cohort, after 1:1 propensity-score matching (1351 men and 1351 women), and in a multivariable Cox model including recorded initial treatment modality; cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray models evaluated adverse liver events. Five-year OS was 24.3% in women and 22.0% in men. Female sex was associated with lower mortality before matching (hazard ratio [HR], 0.90; 95% CI, 0.85-0.97), after matching (HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99; p = 0.024), and after multivariable adjustment (HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.85-0.98; p = 0.010). Male sex was associated with a higher hazard of adverse liver events (cause-specific HR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.43; subdistribution HR [sHR], 1.23; 95% CI, 1.08-1.40). Alcohol-related and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-related HCC had higher liver-event hazards than hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related HCC. For OS, the global sex-by-etiology interaction was not significant ( p = 0.866). Female sex was associated with modestly better outcomes, although the China-dominant cohort limits generalizability.

title: Reevaluation of the role of HBsAg testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility determination.
abstract: The utility of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility screening is uncertain in the era of concurrent hepatitis B virus (HBV) nucleic acid testing (NAT) and hepatitis B core total antibody (anti-HBc) screening. We performed an analysis of 300,112 deceased tissue and cornea donors. screened for eligibility between January 2021 and May 2026. Donors were screened for HBV NAT, HBsAg, and anti-HBc; results were analyzed to characterize HBV screening profiles and evaluate the incremental yield of HBsAg reactivity among donors with nonreactive NAT results. Overall, 97.02% of donors (n=291,180) had HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive results and 0.11% (n=318) of donors had HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-reactive results. In 0.57% of donors (n=1,697) HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-reactive results were obtained and 2.30% of donors (n=6,917) were HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive. Among HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive donors, 97.79% (n=6,764) were also anti-HBc-nonreactive. HBsAg testing identified 22.5 additional reactive screening results (per 1,000 donors) among donors without HBV NAT and anti-HBc reactivity. A subset of reactive HBsAg specimens were evaluated by supplemental confirmatory testing (n=1,131); only 17.28% were confirmed reactive. In this cohort, HBsAg testing identified potential donors for whom the biological significance of HBsAg reactivity remains uncertain, and current eligibility requirements result in donor exclusion.

title: Fusion of deep and handcrafted features from multi-modal ultrasound data for multi-task liver disease diagnosis.
abstract: AIMS: Chronic liver diseases, including fibrosis, inflammation, and steatosis, often coexist and challenge accurate diagnosis. Current approaches either carry procedural risks or fail to provide comprehensive early assessment. This study aims to develop a non-invasive, multimodal ultrasound-based framework for simultaneous grading of all three conditions. METHODS: Our method integrates deep semantic features from deep learning networks with handcrafted features from quantitative ultrasound techniques, capturing complementary information from B-mode images, shear wave elastography, and radio-frequency data. Deep features can reveal discriminable and robust high-dimension non-linear relationships, while handcrafted features can capture ultrasonic characteristics related to the three diseases. These features are fused via a lightweight neural network to predict the probability of different grades of the three diseases, with liver biopsy results serving as the reference standard. The proposed method is evaluated on a cohort of 142 patients with chronic hepatitis B. RESULTS: The proposed method achieves AUCs of 0.86, 0.85, 0.89, and 0.93 for fibrosis staging of ≥ F1, ≥ F2, ≥ F3, and F4, respectively; 0.87 and 0.95 for inflammation grading of ≥ A2 and A3, respectively; and 0.83 and 0.93 for steatosis grading of ≥ S1 and ≥ S2, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed method outperforms existing methods and demonstrates robust performance in both early and advanced disease stages. This multi-task framework has potential as a clinically actionable tool for comprehensive liver disease assessment and decision support.

title: Case of Sclerosing Angiomatoid Nodular Transformation (SANT) in a G6PD Patient: Discussion of Histological Differential Diagnosis.
abstract: Sclerosing angiomatoid nodular transformation (SANT) is a benign entity of the spleen composed of numerous angiomatoid nodules separated by fibrotic and sclerotic stroma. It was first described in 2004, with less than 300 published cases. Radiological findings are not specific and histological examination is needed for the definitive diagnosis of SANT. To further highlight and elucidate the features of this recently described tumour, we herein present a case of this entity and discuss the histological differential diagnosis. The patient is a 51-year-old Chinese male who was incidentally found to have a lesion in the spleen while undergoing surveillance hepatobiliary ultrasound for chronic hepatitis B. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed a 1.8 cm large ill-defined splenic soft tissue nodule. Laparoscopic splenectomy was performed. title: PSMA- and SSTR-targeted imaging and tissue characteristics in woodchuck hepatocellular carcinoma: an exploratory descriptive study
abstract: Abstract Background The use of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)- and somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-targeted radiotheranostics for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) requires preclinical models that reproduce the features of spontaneous tumors. Woodchucks chronically infected with woodchuck hepatitis virus (WHV) develop hepatic tumors that closely resemble hepatitis B virus-induced human HCC. We further characterized PSMA-targeted imaging and normal-tissue expression, including the salivary glands, and evaluated SSTR2/5 expression and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC uptake. We also explored the feasibility and short-term tolerability of a single [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 administration. Results Twelve tumor-bearing woodchucks underwent PET/CT imaging with [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 or [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC (six animals each), with tissue expression assessed by quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemistry. PSMA transcripts were detected in tumors, liver and salivary glands, and PSMA staining was present in tumor-associated microvessels and normal tissues. [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 uptake varied within and between tumors, with a median tumor maximum standardized uptake value of 3.3 and tumor-to-liver ratio of 1.9. Uptake was also observed in salivary glands and other normal organs. Although SSTR2/5 transcripts and cytoplasmic staining were detected in tumors, only one of six animals showed strong [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC tumor uptake relative to liver. HCC was confirmed in all animals at necropsy. Tumors showed heterogeneous contrast enhancement, fibrosis and necrosis, and hepatic lymph node metastases were present in 6 of 10 animals in which lymph nodes were sampled. A single [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 administration and serial follow-up were feasible in three animals; no changes in appetite or activity were observed. Conclusions SSTR-targeted imaging and normal-tissue characterization add to previous PSMA imaging findings in woodchuck HCC. The observed variation in tumor histopathology, target expression and radiopharmaceutical uptake supports further use of this model to study molecular imaging and radiopharmaceutical delivery in spontaneous HCC.

title: 18F-FAPI PET/CT Reveals Intrapatient Biological Heterogeneity in FDG-Negative Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by substantial biological heterogeneity, which may occur between different tumor nodules within the same patient. 18 F-FAPI PET/CT has demonstrated potential advantages over 18 F-FDG PET/CT in the detection of HCC, the biological determinants responsible for heterogeneous FAPI uptake remain incompletely understood. We report a rare case of FDG-negative HCC showing discordant FAPI accumulation between two lesions within the same patient. Case presentation A 53-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B-related cirrhosis underwent surveillance imaging for mildly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (18.70 ng/mL). MRI revealed two suspicious hepatic nodules in segments VIII and VI. Both lesions were negative on 18 F-FDG PET/CT; however, subsequent 18 F-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated markedly heterogeneous uptake, with mild accumulation in the segment VIII lesion (SUVmax 4.1 vs. liver SUVmax 3.5) and intense uptake in the segment VI lesion (SUVmax 12.3). Surgical resection confirmed two HCC lesions with distinct histopathological features and Ki-67 indices (20% and 60%, respectively). Both lesions showed hepatocellular differentiation and microvascular invasion. As FAP immunohistochemistry was unavailable, the mechanism underlying the discordant FAPI uptake remains unclear. Conclusion This case demonstrates substantial interlesional heterogeneity of 18 F-FAPI uptake among multifocal FDG-negative HCCs. The discordant tracer distribution within the same patient suggests that FAPI PET/CT may provide complementary information regarding tumor biological characteristics and microenvironmental differences beyond conventional metabolic imaging.

title: MiR-223 and miR-323 as biomarkers of inflammatory and neuropsychiatric alterations in long COVID with chronic viral hepatitis.
abstract: Long COVID involves persistent physical, mental, and functional symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Its biological mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly with chronic viral hepatitis. This study investigated associations between microRNA (miRNA) expression and mental and physical health outcomes in individuals with Long COVID, considering chronic hepatitis B or C. This cross-sectional study included 80 individuals divided into four groups (n = 20 each): Long COVID, chronic viral hepatitis, Long COVID with hepatitis, and controls. Depression, anxiety, quality of life, fatigue, and functional status were assessed using validated scales, including the Post-COVID Functional Status Scale. Expression of miR-122, miR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations were evaluated using non-parametric tests and correlation analyses. MiR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 were significantly upregulated in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiRNA expression was associated with mental and physical health outcomes, particularly through a positive correlation between miR-323 expression and anxiety levels in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiR-223 was the only miRNA significantly overexpressed in this group compared with all other groups, suggesting its potential as a biomarker of coexisting conditions. Depression and anxiety affected up to 75% and 50% of individuals in the Long COVID groups, respectively (p < 0.05).These findings suggest that circulating miRNAs, particularly miR-223, miR-143, and miR-323, are associated with Long COVID in the presence of chronic viral hepatitis and may serve as biomarkers of disease burden and clinical heterogeneity.

This study investigated associations between microRNA (miRNA) expression and mental and physical health outcomes in individuals with Long COVID, considering chronic hepatitis B or C. This cross-sectional study included 80 individuals divided into four groups (n = 20 each): Long COVID, chronic viral hepatitis, Long COVID with hepatitis, and controls. Depression, anxiety, quality of life, fatigue, and functional status were assessed using validated scales, including the Post-COVID Functional Status Scale. Expression of miR-122, miR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations were evaluated using non-parametric tests and correlation analyses. MiR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 were significantly upregulated in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiRNA expression was associated with mental and physical health outcomes, particularly through a positive correlation between miR-323 expression and anxiety levels in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiR-223 was the only miRNA significantly overexpressed in this group compared with all other groups, suggesting its potential as a biomarker of coexisting conditions. Depression and anxiety affected up to 75% and 50% of individuals in the Long COVID groups, respectively (p < 0.05).These findings suggest that circulating miRNAs, particularly miR-223, miR-143, and miR-323, are associated with Long COVID in the presence of chronic viral hepatitis and may serve as biomarkers of disease burden and clinical heterogeneity.

title: Fertility and course of pregnancy in chronic liver disease
abstract: Chronic liver diseases may affect fertility and pregnancy because of metabolic and hormonal changes. Cirrhosis decreases fertility and increases the risk of maternal and perinatal complications. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is often associated with polycystic ovary syndrome and insulin resistance, which reduces fertility and increases the risk of gestational complications. Women with chronic viral hepatitis B and hepatitis C and autoimmune liver diseases have normal fertility; however, there is an increased risk of gestational implications, as argued in this review.

title: A Pan-Hepatic T-Cell Atlas Identifies Disease-Specific Immune Dysfunction and Therapeutic Targets for Immunotherapy.
abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics has greatly advanced insight into hepatic immunity and immunotherapy. However, the absence of an integrated atlas spanning multiple hepatic diseases limits systematic comparisons of immune heterogeneity and dynamics. Here, we established a Pan-HEpatic single-cell Atlas of T cells (Pheat), covering 139 donors, 255 blood and liver samples spanning chronic hepatitis (chronic hepatitis B/C [CHB/CHC], alcohol-associated hepatitis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis), cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and healthy controls (HC), and delineated profound population-, tissue-, and disease-level heterogeneity of 624,215 T cells, with emphasis on CD8 + exhausted T cells (Tex) and CD4 + regulatory T cells (Treg). Within Tex, intrahepatic precursor Tex (Tex pre ) were depleted in CHB compared with healthy controls and other hepatic diseases. Disease-specific checkpoint dominance (4-1BB in CHB, TIGIT in HCC) in Tex pre was identified and experimentally validated. Panobinostat was predicted and validated to reinvigorate Tex pre in CHB patients. In parallel, effector Treg (eTreg) accumulated in diseased livers and exhibited divergent IL-2-STAT5 signaling-hyperactive in CHB and HCC, suppressed in cirrhosis-indicating distinct immunosuppressive status. Lapatinib/olopatadine enhanced Treg suppressive markers in cirrhosis. Pheat provides a high-resolution atlas of hepatic T cells, revealing disease-specific immune heterogeneity and regulatory programs that inform cellular and molecular targets for potential immunotherapy.

title: Occupational Exposure to N,N-Dimethylformamide and Hepatotoxicity among Synthetic Leather Workers in Bangladesh: Implications for Workplace Health and Labour Law Compliance
abstract: Abstract Purpose : N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) is a polar aprotic solvent that is extensively used in the production of synthetic leather, polyurethane products, resins, adhesives and surface coatings. Potential sources of occupational exposures are mixing, formulation, coating, solvent transfer, cleaning, maintenance, and spill-response. DMF may be inhaled and absorbed through intact skin, which means that total internal dose for a particular worker may be underestimated by only measuring DMF in the air. Liver is a known target organ of DMF toxicity, and reports of increased liver enzymes and, less frequently, clinically significant liver injury have been reported in workers occupationally exposed to DMF. Increases in liver-function tests, however, are non-specific and can occur in people who drink too much alcohol and/or are obese, and/or may be caused by metabolic disease associated with steatotic liver disease, viral hepatitis, certain medicines (prescribed or not) or other exposures that may occur at work. Therefore, a comprehensive evaluation of possible liver damage from DMF should include exposure history, workplace monitoring, biological monitoring, repeated clinical evaluations, and the careful consideration of other causes of liver damage. Objective : The aim of this study is to find the relationship between DMF exposure and liver injury in the workers working in the synthetic leather, polyurethane, resin and surface-coating industries. It will consider exposure by inhalation and skin contact, estimate internal exposure as measured by urinary markers, review liver-function patterns as they change over time, determine if another source of liver injury or exposure may have occurred, and determine if a failure of workplace controls or medical surveillance could have led to exposure. The results will help to inform evidence-based occupational-health and medico-legal decisions about the possibility and level of occupational contribution to liver disease. Methods : An occupational-health study using a mixed-methods approach will be conducted with workers who may be at risk for DMF, such as mixers, formulators, coating operators, solvent-transfer workers, cleaners, maintenance workers, and waste-handling workers. A standardised occupational history will document job titles, length of employment, work patterns, frequency of tasks, use of DMF containing products, past chemical exposures, spillages, symptoms, hygiene practices and use and suitability of personal protective equipment (PPE). Task specific workplace exposure assessments will be carried out and personal air sampling will be used, wherever possible, especially during transfer, mixing, coating, cleaning and maintenance activities. The results of the air-monitoring will be evaluated against relevant occupational exposure concentrations with an understanding that an exposure below the airborne concentration limit does not mean there is no significant dermal absorption. The dermal exposure potential will be evaluated by conducting facility observations and interviews with workers, which will include direct hands-on contact with the material, use of contaminated gloves and clothing, gloves used, gloves replaced, local exhaust ventilation, housekeeping, spill control, washing facility, training, and working practices. The urinary concentrations of N-methylformamide (NMF) and N-acetyl-S-(N-methylcarbamoyl)cysteine (AMCC) will be measured for internal DMF exposure. These are markers of systemic exposure from all routes of exposure including inhalation and skin contact. Ideally, urine samples will be collected at the end of shift and end of work week, or at other suitable times depending on the toxicokinetic properties of the biomarker. Urine dilutions, e.g. creatinine, specific gravity etc., will be corrected and results interpreted taking into account the timing of the sample, the analytical procedure and available biological guidance values. Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels, bilirubin, albumin and international normalised ratio (INR) will be measured at regular intervals. These tests will assist in the identification of hepatocellular, cholestatic or mixed liver injury patterns and be useful in identifying transient, persistent or progressive liver injuries. Symptoms such as fatigue, nausea, abdominal discomfort, jaundice, pruritus and constitutional symptoms will also be recorded. Systematic assessment of potential confounding factors and alternative diagnosis. Alcohol intake, BMI, presence of diabetes, metabolic disease, pre-existing liver disease, other hepatotoxic chemicals and drug or supplement use will be recorded. Investigations may consist of a hepatology specialist review, abdominal ultrasound and hepatitis B and C testing, where clinically appropriate and consented to. There will be a structured medico-legal review, combining evidence from 4 domains – exposure, biological plausibility, individual clinical disease and duty of care. Occupational history and occupational monitoring will support the results of urinary biomarkers as evidence of internal exposure. The adequacy of engineering controls, local exhaust ventilation, training, spill management, hazard communication and medical surveillance will be taken into account in the duty of care assessment. Challenging with the drug after a possible hepatotoxic reaction will not take place. Expected Results : The study will not pre-judge causation as there is currently no data. It is anticipated to see if the workers with high overall or task specific exposure would have higher levels of urinary NMF and AMCC, and if these workers would have more frequent and persistent liver-test abnormalities. It will also be evaluated if liver enzymes improve if DMF exposure is reduced or eliminated, if follow up is available. Importantly, the analysis will differentiate isolated elevations of enzymes from a pattern of occupationally related disease. Conclusions :Concurring inhalational and dermal exposure to DMF is an occupational-health hazard that can be prevented. Task-based exposure assessment, urinary biomarkers, serial liver tests, clinical differential diagnosis and structured medico-legal analysis is a better approach for assessing possible occupational hepatotoxicity than liver enzymes alone. Decisions regarding the possibility, probability and highly probable occupational contribution will be based on the overall evidence and distinct from legal liability.PPE, training, spillage or medical surveillance had a significant impact on the workers.

Task-based exposure assessment, urinary biomarkers, serial liver tests, clinical differential diagnosis and structured medico-legal analysis is a better approach for assessing possible occupational hepatotoxicity than liver enzymes alone. Decisions regarding the possibility, probability and highly probable occupational contribution will be based on the overall evidence and distinct from legal liability.PPE, training, spillage or medical surveillance had a significant impact on the workers.

title: β-Amyrin,an active compound of Bryophyllum pinnatum,alleviates alcoholic liver disease by regulating AKT1 expression and enhancing antioxidant defense.
abstract: Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken (BP), a traditional hepatoprotective herb, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in managing liver disorders. However, the specific bioactive compounds of BP and its mechanisms against alcoholic liver disease (ALD) remain unclear. In this study, the bioactive compounds of BP were screened by database mining and their targets were predicted. A compound-target-disease network was constructed to identify core targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation to validate the binding of β-Amyrin with AKT1. The hepatoprotective efficacy and mechanism were finally verified in ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells. A database screening process has identified four bioactive compounds (β-Amyrin, Astragalin, α-Amyrin and Bryophyllin A). Network pharmacology analyses revealed 138 common targets, primarily associated with lipid metabolism, hepatitis B and C, and the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, and core targets included AKT1, CCND1, EGFR, HIF1A and SRC. Notably, in vitro experiments using ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells demonstrated that β-Amyrin significantly reduced transaminase (ALT, AST), total cholesterol (TC) and triglyceride (TG). Additionally, β-Amyrin enhanced antioxidant defense (SOD, CAT, GSH) and suppressed malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation. Furthermore, β-Amyrin alleviated intracellular lipid accumulation as evidenced by Oil Red O staining. Mechanistically, β-Amyrin restored the expression of total AKT1 and its phosphorylation level (p-AKT1), which could be abolished by AKT1-specific inhibitor MK2206. This is the first study to identify β-Amyrin as the key bioactive compound of BP against ALD, and these findings provide compelling evidence for BP's potential as a therapeutic strategy for ALD.

title: Clinical Significance of Indeterminate Antibody to Hepatitis C in Cancer Patients.
abstract: Most patients with cancer are screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection using an antibody to HCV (anti-HCV) test. However, the importance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result is unknown. We investigated the clinical significance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result in cancer patients. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of cancer patients screened for HCV infection using ARCHITECT Anti-HCV at our institution between October 2016 and July 2024. Patients were categorized based on their anti-HCV results as patients with indeterminate anti-HCV and undetectable HCV-RNA in the absence of HCV treatment, and patients with reactive anti-HCV and chronic infection. We compared the two groups using univariable analyses and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Of the 112,180 patients screened with anti-HCV, 114 (0.1%) had indeterminate results; 101 of them with confirmed cancer were further analysed. Anti-HCV testing was repeated in 24 (24%) patients; most (84%) had non-reactive (46%) or indeterminate (38%) results. Among the 101 patients with indeterminate anti-HCV, 98 (97%) did not have proven HCV infection, but 3 (3%) had HCV infection. Multivariable analysis showed that male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.40-3.53, p < 0.001), age ≥ 60 years (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.01-2.56, p = 0.046), hepatitis B or HIV coinfection (aOR 3.13, 95% CI 1.21-8.11, p = 0.019) and cirrhosis (aOR 6.67, 95% CI 2.05-21.69, p = 0.002) were more likely to have chronic than an indeterminate anti-HCV result. Indeterminate anti-HCV results are uncommon in cancer patients and rarely indicate HCV infection.

title: Global age-specific burden of HBV-related diseases, 1990–2021, with projections to 2050
abstract: BACKGROUND: Universal childhood vaccination has contributed to reductions in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related disease burden among younger populations, but population aging is increasing it in older adults. This study assesses age‐specific global HBV-related disease trends (1990-2021), quantifies drivers, and projects to 2050 to inform optimized prevention strategies. METHODS: We used Global Burden of Disease 2021 data to analyze trends in incidence, prevalence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) for HBV-related diseases from 1990-2021. We stratified analyses by age groups (< 20, 20-54, ≥ 55 years). We quantified contributing drivers using Das Gupta decomposition and mapped geographic patterns by socio-demographic index (SDI). We applied Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling to project future burden through 2050. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2021, global age-standardized incidence, prevalence, death, and DALY rates of HBV-related diseases declined, whereas the absolute numbers of deaths and DALYs increased. Age-stratified analyses showed sharp declines in all burden indicators among individuals < 20 years, while reductions were modest and case numbers increased among those aged 20-54 and, more prominently, ≥ 55 years. Decomposition analysis demonstrated that epidemiological improvements drove reductions in younger populations, whereas population growth and aging offset these gains in older adults. Geographically, the highest burden remained concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia, while high SDI regions maintained the lowest levels. Relative changes indicated substantial global incidence reductions in the < 20 years group, with smaller declines in older groups. Projections suggest that although overall rates will continue to decline, the absolute burden in the ≥ 55 years group will continue to rise through 2050. CONCLUSIONS: Although HBV-related disease burden continues to decline among younger populations, population growth and aging are reshaping the global HBV burden toward individuals aged ≥ 55 years, highlighting the need for targeted prevention and management strategies.

Relative changes indicated substantial global incidence reductions in the < 20 years group, with smaller declines in older groups. Projections suggest that although overall rates will continue to decline, the absolute burden in the ≥ 55 years group will continue to rise through 2050. Although HBV-related disease burden continues to decline among younger populations, population growth and aging are reshaping the global HBV burden toward individuals aged ≥ 55 years, highlighting the need for targeted prevention and management strategies.

title: False‐Positive Hepatitis C Virus Serology Following HeartMate 3 Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
abstract: ABSTRACT Background False‐positive hepatitis C virus (HCV) (FPHC) serology has been reported with earlier‐generation axial‐flow left ventricular assist devices (LVADs), but its frequency with the magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 and its implications for heart transplant pathways remain unknown. This study describes FPHC serology in HeartMate 3 LVAD recipients and explores associated clinical and immunological features. Methods A retrospective, single‐center study was conducted at a specialist cardiothoracic center. All adults implanted with a HeartMate 3 LVAD between March 2018 and July 2025 with complete HCV serology before and after implantation were included. Patients developing HCV antibody positivity with negative confirmatory testing were classified as having FPHC serology. Patient demographics, blood product transfusions, liver function tests, lactate dehydrogenase, and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) sensitization were compared between groups. Results Among 54 HeartMate 3 LVAD recipients, 10 (18.5%) developed FPHC serology after implantation. There were no significant differences between groups in age, sex, liver function tests, or lactate dehydrogenase. The number of fresh frozen plasma units transfused at implantation and the development of anti‐HLA Class I antibodies were associated with FPHC serology ( p = 0.039, p = 0.04, respectively). No significant associations were observed with red blood cell or platelet transfusions. Conclusion FPHC serology is a clinically important phenomenon in HeartMate 3 LVAD recipients. Clinicians and patients should be aware of this phenomenon to minimize unnecessary investigations and delays to transplant candidacy assessment. Standardized confirmatory testing protocols and multicenter studies are needed to clarify the underlying immune mechanisms and their impact on post‐transplant outcomes.

title: Prevalence and outcomes of co-occurring mental/physical comorbidities and substance use disorders: An atlas umbrella review including 156 systematic reviews with meta-analysis
abstract: Substance use disorders(SUDs) are intertwined with psychiatric and general medical disorders. Substances of abuse also exert intrinsic toxicities and adverse effects that contribute to extensive somatic multimorbidity, complicating patient prognoses. This umbrella review(UR) systematically aggregated, harmonized, and graded the credibility of meta-analytic evidence concerning SUD comorbidities across psychiatric/somatic dimensions. We searched major electronic databases up to July 2026 for systematic reviews with meta-analyses of observational studies mapping SUD co-occurrences. Extracted data were categorized by ICD-11 diagnostic blocks. Meta-analytic estimates were evaluated using pre-registered quantitative credibility indicators assessing sample size(N), number of studies(k), 95%confidence interval(95%CI) widths, and heterogeneity(I 2 ). The review included 156 systematic reviews with meta-analysis, encompassing 100,441,167 database/registry records across 14,322 study entries, with possible overlap across reviews. High-credibility data showed a strong intra-block psychiatric overlap: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder demonstrated a pooled SUD prevalence of 21.0%(95%CI=17.0-25.0%;k = 31), while Major Depressive Disorder reached a prevalence of 36.1%(95%CI=32.4%-39.7%;k = 161) among patients with Opioid Use Disorder(OUD). Somatic toxicities and iatrogenic pathways were highly prevalent: opioid analgesic use in chronic noncancer pain 27.0%(95%C.I.=23.0-31.0%;N > 3.9 M), and in post-lumbar fusion surgery patients (40.0%;95%C.I.=32.0-49.0%). High prevalences of syndemic infectious comorbidities were observed among populations with injection drug use, with Hepatitis C virus prevalence reaching 61.0%(95%CI=56.0-67.0%) in regional cohorts. Highly specific associations revealed that schizotypal traits strongly correlate with Cannabis Use Disorder(I 2 =0%). SUDs are multi-systemic disorders characterized by substantial cross-block psychiatric/medical multimorbidity. The breadth and the credibility gradient of multimorbidity argue for routine cross-domain screening and coordinated care, with model effectiveness left to trials.

title: Quasispecies relocate rather than drift: hierarchical genotype networks track viral adaptation
abstract: Viral populations are ensembles of mutationally related genotypes that explore sequence space locally. Their genotype networks are hierarchical: abundance decays with mutational distance from the most abundant genotype (the root) and degree distributions are heavy-tailed. How this architecture responds to selective challenges remains unclear. We combine simulations of sequence populations on NK fitness landscapes with longitudinal hepatitis B virus (HBV) deep-sequencing data from chronically infected patients under treatment. Quasispecies structure is rapidly rebuilt around the current root, while root replacement is occasional, when a fitter variant is found. Adaptation unfolds on two timescales: fast, local reorganisation and slow, stochastic relocation. HBV populations of patients not responding to therapy show stasis. Meanwhile, responders show either near-complete replacement by a new root, or transient excursions followed by return to the original root. These patterns resemble the stasis and relocation regimes found in simulations. Our results suggest that genotype network organization and dynamics under selective pressure present generic features of molecular adaptation, with a potentially informative clinical readout.

source_records.abstract: Viral populations are ensembles of mutationally related genotypes that explore sequence space locally. Their genotype networks are hierarchical: abundance decays with mutational distance from the most abundant genotype (the root) and degree distributions are heavy-tailed. How this architecture responds to selective challenges remains unclear. We combine simulations of sequence populations on NK fitness landscapes with longitudinal hepatitis B virus (HBV) deep-sequencing data from chronically infected patients under treatment. Quasispecies structure is rapidly rebuilt around the current root, while root replacement is occasional, when a fitter variant is found. Adaptation unfolds on two timescales: fast, local reorganisation and slow, stochastic relocation. HBV populations of patients not responding to therapy show stasis. Meanwhile, responders show either near-complete replacement by a new root, or transient excursions followed by return to the original root. These patterns resemble the stasis and relocation regimes found in simulations. Our results suggest that genotype network organization and dynamics under selective pressure present generic features of molecular adaptation, with a potentially informative clinical readout.

title: Association of Aldehyde Dehydrogenase 2 ( ALDH2 ) rs671 Polymorphism and Alcohol-Related Liver Outcomes in Studies from China and Taiwan: A Systematic Review
abstract: Alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) is a major public health concern in East Asia, where alcohol consumption and genetic susceptibility jointly influence disease risk. This systematic review evaluated the association between aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) polymorphisms, alcoholism, and ALD susceptibility among Chinese and Taiwanese populations. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science and identified 1,743 records, followed by PRISMA guidelines. After screening and eligibility assessment were conducted, nine studies comprising 3,586 cases from China and Taiwan were included. Evidence was categorized into ALD severity, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and longitudinal outcomes. Associations were summarized using odds ratios (ODs), Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE) was reassessed, overlapping reports were carefully considered, and bias was calculated. Individuals carrying ALDH2 polymorphisms showed an increased risk of ALD, odds ratio 2.28 (95% Cl: 1.01–5.15. Significant associations were observed for cirrhosis (ODs = 2.02, 95% Cl:1.10–3.71), HCC (ODs = 19.59, 95% Cl: 4.38-87.68), and hepatitis B-related liver disease (ODs = 5.59, 95% Cl: 2.42–12.90). The association was stronger among studies from China (ODs = 4.00, 95% Cl:1.74–9.20), whereas the Taiwan subgroup showed a lower frequency of the genetic variant in liver disease associated with chronic alcohol consumption cases. Allele frequencies and drinking behaviors were observed between the two countries. Taiwanese populations have lower frequencies of the ALDH2 Glu and one variant Lys allele, and higher rates of alcohol dependence and liver disease compared with Chinese populations. The interaction of genetic predisposition, alcohol consumption, and sociocultural factors appears to play an important role in ALD progression.

title: The Nucleoside Analogue NITD008 , Alone or Combined With Ribavirin, Potently Reduces Hepatitis E Virus Infection in Humanised Mice
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection is becoming increasingly clinically relevant worldwide, but no approved antiviral therapy currently exists. Ribavirin (RBV) is used off‐label for immunosuppressed patients with chronic hepatitis E, although it is effective in only 80% of patients and linked to side effects. The nucleoside analogue NITD008 was shown to be effective against a broad range of RNA viruses. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy of NITD008, alone or in combination with RBV, in humanised mice stably infected with HEV. Methods Mice received either NITD008 alone (20 mg/Kg/day) by oral gavage for up to 2 weeks, or 5 mg/Kg NITD008 alone or in combination with RBV (50 mg/Kg). Viral changes were determined in faeces, blood and intrahepatically. Results NITD008 efficiently reduced HEV loads to undetectable levels in serum and by > 4log 10 in faeces within 1 week. Intrahepatic analysis showed a ∆log 10 : 2.5 reduction in HEV RNA levels in treated mice compared to controls after 2 weeks. Imaging showed fewer HEV‐RNA‐positive human hepatocytes in treated mice. NITD008 did not increase serum markers of hepatocyte death. Combination therapy induced stronger suppression of HEV RNA in faeces (∆log 10 : 5.02) than RBV monotherapy (∆log 10 : 1.08), despite lower NITD008 doses. Conclusions This study demonstrates the non‐toxicity of NITD008 towards human hepatocytes and more potent antiviral activity compared to RBV in HEV‐infected mice. Combination regimens with RBV showed strong additive activity. The study suggests that HEV clearance may be achieved in immunosuppressed patients by using and further developing this class of direct antiviral drugs.

title: Development and validation of a prediction model for multidrug-resistant infection in patients with HBV-related acute-on-chronic liver failure complicated by bacterial infection: a dual-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial infections significantly increase mortality in patients with hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF). This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model based on clinical indicators at the time of infection onset to early identify high-risk patients for MDR infection and guide empirical antimicrobial therapy. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 191 patients with HBV-ACLF and bacterial infection, divided into MDR ( n = 125) and non-MDR ( n = 66) groups. Clinical and etiological data were collected at the time of infection onset. Candidate variables were initially screened by univariate logistic regression and clinical relevance, followed by Spearman correlation analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression for feature selection. A multivariable logistic regression model was constructed, and a nomogram was developed. Internal validation was performed using the bootstrap method (1000 resamples) and 10-fold cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results A total of 191 pathogenic strains were isolated, including 111 (58.1%) Gram-negative and 80 (41.9%) Gram-positive bacteria. title: Survival outcomes of liver cancer patients at a tertiary care cancer center, India: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has poor survival due to late diagnosis. This study estimated five-year overall survival and factors associated with mortality among HCC patients. Methods This retrospective cohort study included patients with confirmed HCC registered at Tata Memorial Centre during 2018–2019. Clinical variables, including alcohol use, hepatitis status, cirrhosis, biomarkers, and staging by the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) system, were extracted from electronic medical records. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method, and independent determinants using multivariable Cox regression, with hazard ratios re-estimated using inverse probability weighting to account for loss to follow-up. STATA v15.0 was used for statistical analysis. Results Among 1,025 HCC patients (mean age 56.95 ± 12.58 years), 879 (85.76%) were male. Liver cirrhosis was present in 545 (53.17%) patients, hepatitis B infection in 457 (44.59%), and alcohol use in 268 (26.15%). BCLC stage C was seen in 402 (39.22%) patients and stage D in 92 (8.98%), while 815 (79.51%) had moderate impairment. Median overall survival was 10.81 months (1-, 3-, 5-year: 48.17%, 25.72%, 17.75%). Females survived longer than males (17.35 vs. 9.79 months; p=0.03). Survival declined progressively from BCLC stage A to stage D (54.57 to 3.42 months; p<0.001). On weight-adjusted analysis, alcohol use (aHR=1.40), hepatitis B (aHR=1.69), severe impairment (aHR=4.78), and BCLC stage D (aHR=2.88) independently predicted mortality. Combination therapy was associated with improved survival (aHR=0.52) compared with no treatment (aHR=1.44). Conclusion HCC patients in this cohort had poor overall survival, underscoring the need for earlier diagnosis and timely, stage-appropriate treatment to improve outcomes.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-Triggered Dual-Mode Electrochemical and Raman-Silent Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Biosensing for Sensitive HBV DNA Detection
abstract: Abstract Sensitive and reliable quantification of hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA is important for monitoring viral replication and therapeutic response. Electrochemical (EC) sensing offers simple quantitative readout, but resolving current changes at low target concentrations remains challenging. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), in contrast, provides signal amplification but generally requires specialized optical instrumentation and may suffer from matrix interference. To accommodate different analytical requirements, we developed a CRISPR/Cas12a-triggered dual-mode EC/SERS biosensing platform. This platform integrates a conductive/plasmonic gold nanoparticles (Au NPs)/copper(II)-2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (Cu3(HHTP)2)/indium tin oxide (ITO) interface with a CRISPR-responsive DNA hydrogel. The hydrogel serves as a target-responsive interfacial gate, with Cas12a-mediated cleavage regulating electrode accessibility to facilitate EC transduction and promote plasmonic coupling between SERS tags and Au NPs. Ag@Au nanocubes functionalized with 4-mercaptobenzonitrile were employed as SERS tags, providing a characteristic CN signal at 2228 cm−1 in the Raman-silent region. The EC mode exhibited a linear response to the logarithm of HBV DNA concentration from 100 fM to 10 nM, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 17.1 fM. The SERS mode was evaluated in parallel on a separate, identically prepared hydrogel-modified electrode, yielding a linear range of 5 fM to 1 nM and an LOD of 0.143 fM. This platform combines the operational simplicity and quantitative capability of EC sensing with the high sensitivity of SERS detection, providing complementary readout options for different HBV DNA testing requirements.

title: Association between low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and the presence of cholelithiasis among hospitalized people living with HIV: a retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: Dyslipidemia is common among people living with Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), but evidence on the association between low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and cholelithiasis in this specific population remains limited. We assessed the association between LDL-C and imaging-confirmed cholelithiasis among hospitalized people living with HIV (PLWH). This single-center retrospective analytical cross-sectional study included 259 hospitalized PLWH admitted between January 2019 and January 2025. All participants underwent abdominal imaging during the index hospitalization and had LDL-C measured within 24–48 h of admission. Participants were classified according to the presence ( n = 98) or absence ( n = 161) of imaging-confirmed cholelithiasis. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs), and modified Poisson regression with robust variance was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs). Model I was adjusted for sex, age, and body mass index (BMI), whereas Model II was additionally adjusted for hepatitis B virus (HBV) co-infection, albuvirtide (ABT) treatment, duration since confirmed HIV diagnosis, and CD4 + T-cell count. Expanded adjustment, extreme-value, flexible-curve, breakpoint, and bootstrap analyses were performed as sensitivity or exploratory analyses. Among 259 participants, 98 (37.84%) had imaging-confirmed cholelithiasis and 161 (62.16%) had no imaging evidence of cholelithiasis. Participants with cholelithiasis were younger (50.22 [11.71] vs. 56.30 [16.00] years) and more often female (40.82% vs. 6.21%), and had higher mean LDL-C levels (3.08 [0.96] vs. 2.42 [0.75] mmol/L). Each 1-mmol/L higher LDL-C level was associated with greater odds of cholelithiasis in the fully adjusted logistic model (adjusted OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.79–4.11; P < 0.001) and a higher prevalence in the modified Poisson model (adjusted PR 1.40, 95% CI 1.24–1.59; P < 0.001). The positive association persisted in expanded-adjustment and extreme-value analyses. Flexible models produced model-dependent evidence of nonlinearity, and the data-derived breakpoint showed substantial sampling uncertainty. Among hospitalized PLWH who underwent abdominal imaging, higher LDL-C levels were associated with the presence of cholelithiasis. Because LDL-C and cholelithiasis were assessed during the same hospitalization, temporal order, causality, and future risk cannot be established. The possible nonlinear pattern and breakpoint remain exploratory, require independent validation, and should not guide clinical cut-offs. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Prognostic value of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab: real-world data from Vietnam
abstract: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a standard systemic regimen for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Accessible prognostic indicators are valuable in real-world practice, particularly in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-predominant populations. To evaluate the prognostic value of pretreatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and explore a clinically interpretable threshold for risk stratification. This retrospective, single-center study included 233 patients with advanced HCC treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab at the Vietnam National Cancer Hospital (February 2020-April 2026; follow-up censored June 17, 2026). Candidate NLR thresholds were generated from the literature, cohort distribution, and an exploratory 0.1-increment grid from 2.0 to 5.0, then evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox models. Bootstrap resampling was used to assess internal stability of the selected fixed model; the cutoff-selection process was not repeated within bootstrap samples. Median patient age was 59 years; 91.4% were male, 72.5% had HBV etiology, and 31.3% met real-world trial-ineligibility criteria (IMbrave150-OUT). Median follow-up was 17.35 months, with 125 deaths and 181 progression/death events. Median baseline NLR was 2.34 (IQR, 1.71–3.73). Continuous NLR was associated with OS and PFS in univariable linear Cox analysis; however, adjusted restricted cubic spline analysis did not demonstrate a significant OS association or a non-linear inflection point. NLR ≥ 3.6 stratified median OS (15.64 vs. 10.02 months; p < 0.001) and median PFS (4.34 vs. 3.25 months; p = 0.039). In the final complete-case Cox model (n = 211), NLR ≥ 3.6 was associated with OS (adjusted HR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.13–2.66; p = 0.012) and PFS (adjusted HR, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.05–2.14; p = 0.025). In 500 bootstrap resamples, NLR ≥ 3.6 retained p < 0.05 in 69.0% of OS models and 58.0% of PFS models; optimism-corrected C-indices were 0.599 for OS and 0.549 for PFS. Pretreatment NLR ≥ 3.6 may serve as a pragmatic adjunctive risk-stratification marker in real-world patients with HCC receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab. Because the threshold was cohort-derived and model discrimination was modest, it should not be considered a standalone prediction tool or a biologically definitive cutoff. External validation is required before clinical implementation. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an easily accessible biomarker obtained from routine blood tests. In this real-world study of 233 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab, we explored candidate NLR thresholds using Kaplan-Meier analysis and clinically grounded multivariable Cox models. The cutoff of NLR ≥3.6 was not prespecified; it was derived within this cohort and should be interpreted as exploratory. NLR ≥3.6 was selected as a pragmatic risk-stratification threshold because it separated overall survival and progression-free survival and remained associated with outcomes in the selected categorical Cox model. Bootstrap assessment showed moderate internal stability and modest model discrimination, supporting cautious interpretation and the need for external validation.

title: Reductions in Advanced Chronic Liver Disease Among People Who Inject Drugs: The ETHOS Engage Study.
abstract: Background and aims Liver disease is a significant risk for people who inject drugs due to the high burden of hepatitis C virus (HCV). There is limited data on the impact of the direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy era on liver disease among people who inject drugs. This study evaluated baseline and longitudinal liver disease in a national cohort of people who inject drugs recruited over three Waves: 2018-2019, 2019-2021, and 2023-2025. Methods The ETHOS Engage Study is an observational cohort of people who inject drugs attending drug treatment clinics and needle and syringe programs in Australia. Participants completed a questionnaire and underwent point-of-care HCV RNA testing (Xpert HCV Viral Load Fingerstick) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient hepatic elastography (FibroScan). Advanced chronic liver disease was defined by LSM of 10 kPa or above. Results Among all enrolments with a valid LSM (n = 3126, 79% recruited at drug treatment clinics), 11% had advanced chronic liver disease, decreasing from 12.0% (154/1287) in 2018-2019 to 7.9% (66/839) in 2019-2021, and 6.4% (62/967) in 2023-2025. In adjusted analyses, participants recruited between 2019-2021 and 2023-2025 were less likely to have advanced chronic liver disease (vs. 2018-2019; aOR 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.90 and aOR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.40-0.77, respectively). Current HCV infection declined from 24% in 2018-2019 to 10% in 2023-2025. Among participants with LSM in more than one wave and current HCV infection at first visit and no current HCV infection at second visit (n = 44), advanced chronic liver disease declined from 19% to 5%. Conclusions Unrestricted access to DAA therapies in Australia has been associated with reduced liver disease burden among people who inject drugs. Monitoring of liver health in this population is important, given potential ageing and non-HCV liver disease impacts.

title: Machine learning model using contrast-enhanced CT for predicting overall survival in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE plus targeted and immunotherapy: a multicenter study
abstract: The aim of this study was to develop and validate a machine learning model based on contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) for predicting the overall survival (OS) in unresectable HCC patients treated with TACE combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) plus molecular targeted therapies (MTTs). This study retrospectively reviewed 180 unresectable HCC patients who received TACE-ICIs-MTTs therapy from 4 medical centers. The study comprised of training cohort ( n = 93), internal validation cohort ( n = 39) and external validation cohort ( n = 48). A series of analyses and kinds of models were conducted to build a Radscore. Then, models were constructed using Radscore and clinical variables selected through multivariate Cox regression analysis, evaluated by the Harrell’s concordance index (C-index) and the area under the curve (AUC). The radiomics-clinical model was further assessed by decision curve and calibration curve analysis. The Radscore was derived from 6 features selected by the optimal model (Lasso Cox + RSF with the highest C-index of 0.777). HBV infection and vascular invasion are clinical independent predictors of OS. The radiomics-clinical model demonstrated favorable performance. It achieved C-index values of 0.893(0.859–0.927), 0.758 (0.657–0.86) and 0.74 (0.624–0.856) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. In the external validation cohort, the AUCs achieved 0.731 (0.569–0.893), 0.7 (0.515–0.885), and 0.756 (0.569–0.943) for predicting 1-, 2-, and 3-year outcomes, respectively. The machine learning model based on CECT exhibited favorable performance in predicting overall survival in unresectable HCC patients treated with TACE-ICIs-MTTs, showing potential to identify likely responders and guide treatment decision-making.

title: Diamond-mediated immunosensing of Alpha-l-Fructosidase for diagnosing hepatocellular carcinoma: signal enhancement over conventional ELISA
abstract: Abstract Objectives Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the deadliest liver cancer, a frequent complication that originates from the liver. The common cause of HCC is the infection by Hepatitis B and C. Early diagnosis of liver cancer biomarker helps for providing a better treatment and increase the survival rate. Alpha-L-Fucosidases (AFU) is identified as a potential biomarker for HCC, in particular for detecting smaller tumours. Methods This study develops an improved enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) on diamond nanomaterial modified polystyrene surface (PS). Diamond was modified on ELISA well through carbonyldiimidazole chemical modification and then aptamer was attached on the diamond through the biotin-streptavidin interaction. Results Diamond improves the aptamer attachment on PS well and enhances the interaction of AFU with aptamer and antibody. The limit of detection (LOD) of AFU was calculated to be 25 pg/mL based on a linear regression [y=0.0795× - 0.0857; R 2 =0.967], while the limit of quantification (LOQ) was at 85 pg/mL, which were lower than that achieved by the conventional ELISA method. Conclusions In addition, AFU spiked serum increases the absorbance with enhancing AFU, indicating the selective AFU detection and control molecules did not show the significant absorbance proves the specific AFU detection.

title: Molecular epidemiology of hepatitis C virus and resistance to direct-acting antivirals in tuberculosis patients of Western Siberia (Tomsk Region)
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis C virus infection and tuberculosis represent two major infectious disease burdens worldwide, with co-infection posing particular clinical challenges. The advent of direct-acting antivirals targeting hepatitis C virus (HCV) non-structural proteins NS3, NS5A, and NS5B has transformed hepatitis C treatment, achieving viral eradication in over 95% of patients. However, the emergence of resistance-associated substitutions (RAS) threatens treatment efficacy, particularly in vulnerable populations such as tuberculosis patients, who face elevated risks of drug-induced liver injury and complex drug interactions. Objective To assess the prevalence, genetic diversity, and presence of RAS in HCV isolates circulating among infected patients residing in the Tomsk Region of Russia. Materials and methods A total of 308 serum samples were collected from tuberculosis patients with confirmed HCV RNA positivity. HCV subtypes and recombinant form were determined by phylogenetic analysis of core region and NS5B region sequences which were obtained via Sanger sequencing. For a part of subtype 1b ( n = 29) and 3a ( n = 57) isolates, full-genome or targeted NS3, NS5A, and NS5B sequences were obtained via Illumina next-generation sequencing, followed by RAS analysis. Results Four HCV subtypes and one recombinant form were identified: 1b (43.5%), 3a (42.2%), 1a (12.3%), 2a (1.0%), 2k/1b (1.0%). The study yielded the following baseline RAS frequency data depending on the subtype. NS3: A166S/T (21.1%) was detected among subtype 3a isolates; Y56F (10.3%), S122G (10.3%) and V170I (13.8%) were detected among subtype 1b isolates. NS5A: A30K/S (5.3%), Q/S62L (12.3%) and Y93H (1.8%) were detected among subtype 3a isolates; among the subtype 1b isolates, R30Q (3.4%), L31M (3.4%), P58S (3.4%), and Y93H (3.4%) were detected. NS5B: among the subtype 3a isolates, A150V (40.4%) and K206E (22.8%) were detected; among the subtype 1b isolates, L159F (37.9%), C316N (48.3%), M414L (3.4%), and S556G (24.1%) were detected.

title: Real-World Effectiveness and Safety of Sofosbuvir-Based Therapy in Chinese Children and Adolescents With Chronic HCV Infection: A Retrospective Multicentre Study.
abstract: Few direct-acting antiviral regimens are approved in China for children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and data are limited on their efficacy and safety in this population. This retrospective, multi-centre study aimed to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (LDV/SOF) and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) in Chinese paediatric patients. The study included patients aged 3-17 years from five hospitals across China who received either LDV/SOF or SOF/VEL for chronic HCV infection. The outcomes included the proportion of patients who achieved sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12), normalisation rates of ALT and AST levels, and incidence of adverse events (AEs). A total of 129 patients from five sites were included and 128 completed 12 weeks of post-treatment follow-up. Mean age was 9.9 years (standard deviation, 3.9), with 30 (23.3%), 55 (42.6%), and 44 (34.1%) patients aged 3-6, 7-11, and 12-17 years, respectively, 84 (65.1%) were male, 62 (48.1%) were infected with genotype 3, and baseline ALT and AST levels were elevated in 64 (49.6%) and 75 (58.1%) patients, respectively. The SVR12 rate was 98.4% (126/128) in the overall population, remaining consistent across subgroups by sex, age, HCV genotype, or regimen. ALT and AST levels were normalised in all patients with available data. AEs were reported by 16.4% (21/128) of patients and none were serious. Collectively, this study demonstrated that LDV/SOF and SOF/VEL were highly effective and well tolerated in Chinese paediatric patients with chronic HCV infection.

title: Associations Between Self-Reported Previous Hepatitis C Diagnosis, Hepatitis C Treatment, and Current Binge Drinking Among Persons Who Inject Drugs-National HIV Behavioural Surveillance, 2015-2024.
abstract: Persons who inject drugs (PWID) are disproportionately affected by hepatitis C virus (HCV). Excessive alcohol use among PWID can lead to more rapid progression of liver disease among persons with HCV. We assessed associations between ever reporting HCV infection, ever reporting HCV treatment, and current binge drinking among PWID who participated in National HIV Behavioural Surveillance (NHBS) during 2015-2024. NHBS conducted biobehavioural surveys among PWID using respondent-driven sampling in 2015, 2018, 2022, and 2024. We estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the association between self-report of ever having HCV infection, HCV treatment, and binge drinking in the past 30 days. The percentage of PWID reporting binge drinking was 25.8% in 2015, 24.0% in 2018, 13.3% in 2022, and 17.2% in 2024. In adjusted analysis, we found a significant negative relationship between self-reported ever having HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days in three of the four surveys: 2018 (aPR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.83-0.99), 2022 (aPR: 0.79, 95% CI:0.70-0.90), and 2024 (aPR:0.78, 95% CI: 0.65-0.93). We did not find significant associations between previously ever receiving treatment for HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days across the four survey years. Among PWID, HCV infection was associated with reduced prevalence of binge drinking in 2018, 2022, and 2024. Our results support the importance of testing PWID for HCV infection and continued education on the harms associated with excessive alcohol use, including among persons who have received treatment for HCV infection.

title: Vaccination among older adults in Vietnam: a scoping review protocol
abstract: Objective: This scoping review will map the evidence from Vietnam on vaccination among adults aged 60 years and older: vaccination outcomes, the factors associated with them, interventions to increase vaccination, and costs. Introduction: Vietnamese law defines older people as those aged 60 years and older, and the 2026 national recommendations list eight vaccine groups for this age group, of which only some are publicly funded. Existing reviews cover influenza alone or pool studies from many countries; none maps the Vietnamese evidence across vaccines. Inclusion criteria: Participants are adults aged 60 years and older, or subgroups whose lower age bound is 60 or more, and health workers or caregivers in relation to older adults’ vaccination. The concept covers uptake, intention, acceptance and hesitancy; associated factors; interventions; and costs, willingness to pay and economic evaluations, for influenza, pneumococcal, herpes zoster, diphtheria–tetanus with or without pertussis, hepatitis B, meningococcal, respiratory syncytial virus and dengue vaccines. The context is Vietnam, in any setting. Primary studies of any design published in peer-reviewed journals from 2010 onward, in English or Vietnamese, are eligible. Methods: The review follows the JBI methodology and will be reported with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar, WHO Global Index Medicus, Vietnam Journals Online and nine Vietnamese journals will be searched. Two reviewers will screen records independently; one will chart the data and a second will verify them. Associated factors will be classified by the WHO Behavioural and Social Drivers of Vaccination framework. Results will be presented as counts, tables and an evidence map, without pooling.

title: Segment feature classification method for hepatocellular carcinoma detection from CT images
abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) is a chronic liver cancer triggered by hepatitis B or C identified by abdominal pain and jaundice. Computed Tomography (CT) images are used to analyze the type of HCC as primary or solitary based on the infected ratio. This detection and classification utilize machine learning and correlation datasets for precise diagnosis outcomes. In this article, a Segment Feature Classification Method using Region Normalization (SFCM-RN) is introduced. The proposed method identifies heterogeneity measures between the extracted features under two differentiations: the normal and infected regions. The segmentation process is pursued based on null or fewer heterogeneity measures. The differentiations per region are normalized to identify the infection ratio that increases the classifications. Hence this differentiation to normalization case is iteratively verified using sectional deep learning where the single connected layer performs both normalization to differentiation and vice-versa. The iteration is halted if the maximum infected rate is identified through training inputs. The proposed method improves accuracy, F1-score, recall, and precision by 15.52%, 12.51%, 11.24%, and 11.98% respectively. The proposed method reduces error by 14.51% for the maximum feature set.

title: Genome sequences of hepatitis E virus genotype 1e from an outbreak in the Central African Republic, 2018
abstract: ABSTRACT The hepatitis E virus (HEV) causes major outbreaks in sub-Saharan Africa. Here, we present four genome sequences of HEV-1e from the 2018 outbreak in the Central African Republic. Despite high identity with known African isolates, these sequences constitute a new cluster and suggest local transmission and diversification.

title: Hepadnavirus tropism determined by diversified NTCP functionality in Feline species
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) exhibits a narrow host range, largely determined by sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptides (NTCP), a hepatic bile acid transporter acting as the HBV receptor. NTCP among animals appears to have evolved following trade-off mutations to lose its viral receptor activity while preserving its transporter function. Here, through profiling of the NTCP homologs from 23 mammalian species, we uncover unexpected functional heterogeneity of feline NTCPs. NTCPs derived from cat, tiger, and leopard supported viral preS1 binding and HBV infection, whereas lion-NTCP was deficient for preS1 binding and, notably, exhibited markedly reduced bile acid transport. Cat-NTCP was further demonstrated to have viral receptor function by productive infection in primary cat hepatocytes. Experimental mutagenesis identified double substitution at positions 191 and 268 as key determinants: introducing lion-type substitutions into cat-NTCP (G191R and T268A) abolished preS1 binding, whereas reciprocal substitutions in lion-NTCP restored receptor function. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that lion-NTCP adopts conformation in which a transmembrane helix bending enlarges the whole bile acid tunnel and disrupts preS1 compatibility. Such differences also determined host susceptibility to another feline-infected domestic cat HBV. These findings reveal diversified NTCP functionality with evolutionary plasticity that acquires resistance to hepadnavirus infection at the expense of physiological transporter function.

title: Prevalence of anti-HCV and incidence rate of HCV seroconversion in a large multiregional health check-up population in China: a cross-sectional and longitudinal study of 1.6 million adults.
abstract: Background China carries one of the heaviest burdens of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection worldwide. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of anti-HCV and incidence rate of HCV seroconversion in a large health check-up population in China. Methods This cross-sectional, and longitudinal study used data from the Meinian health check-up database, covering participants from all 31 provinces of mainland China between 2017 and 2023. Serological samples were tested for anti-HCV using ELISA. The weighted prevalence of anti-HCV and the incidence rate of HCV seroconversion were calculated. Poisson regression was used to identify risk factors for HCV seroconversion. Results A total of 1,610,735 participants were included in the analysis of anti-HCV prevalence. The prevalence of anti-HCV in the study population was 0.89% (95% CI, 0.77%-1.01%), with significantly higher prevalence found in females and elderly individuals. Geographically, the prevalence was significantly higher in Central and West China compared to East China. Individuals with abnormal liver function or liver fibrosis, abnormal thyroid function or antibodies, diabetes, and impaired kidney function had significantly higher prevalence. The analysis of HCV seroconversion included 179,447 participants, showing an incidence rate of 0.72 per 1,000 person-years during a median follow-up of 1.5 years. Risk factors for HCV seroconversion included older age, as well as living in Central or West China, border regions, areas with low GDP per capita, and areas with high anti-HCV prevalence. Conclusions Our study reveals significant anti-HCV seroprevalence burden and ongoing risk of HCV transmission in a large health check-up population in China, highlighting the urgent need for systematic screening and enhanced prevention efforts to control HCV transmission.
