title: Structural basis of hypervariable region 1 dynamics on HCV envelope glycoproteins in immune evasion.
abstract: The hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) of the hepatitis C virus E1E2 glycoprotein plays a crucial role in immune evasion through rapid mutation and shielding of conserved neutralizing epitopes. Despite its important role, the structural properties of HVR1 remain poorly understood, particularly how its conformation influences shielding mechanisms and receptor recognition. To date in all published E1E2 or E2 structures, the C-terminal part of HVR1 (394 to 411) remains unresolved. Using neutralizing antibody (nAb) RM1-38, which targets C-terminal HVR1 (residues 399 to 409), we investigated the folding, positioning, flexibility, and shielding function of the RM1-38 epitope, or antigenic site 399 (AS399), on HVR1 by X-ray crystallography and negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM). The crystal structure of RM1-38 Fab with the HVR1 AS399 peptide, combined with mutagenesis analysis, delineated the molecular basis of its strain-specific recognition and neutralization. nsEM and competition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay revealed that HVR1 exhibits pronounced conformational flexibility even in the presence of other nAbs bound to E1E2. Virus neutralization assays using a combination of RM1-38 and broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) demonstrated antagonistic effects of RM1-38 with the bnAbs. Furthermore, RM1-38 reduced E1E2 binding to cells expressing the scavenger receptor SR-BI, an HVR1-dependent receptor, but did not affect binding to CD81 tetraspanin. Together, these findings support a model in which HVR1 functions as a dynamic shield, where its conformational plasticity contributes to both receptor engagement and evasion of humoral immunity in persistent infection.

title: Small Molecules Engineered to Trigger Virus-like Particle Disassembly
abstract: Abstract A molecular delivery system needs to release, as well as package, cargo. In previous work, technology has been described for packaging cargo into virus-like particles (VLPs) based on the Hepatitis B Virus capsid. Here, we describe a panel of dansyl maleimides (DM) designed to trigger VLP disassembly in response to a reducing environment. The VLP is stabilized by protein–protein interactions and also disulfide cross-links between the C-terminal cysteine of each capsid protein (Cp). The DM molecules react with a second cysteine, buried at the Cp-Cp interface. The DMs, of varying size, disrupt Cp-Cp interactions, leaving VLPs held together primarily by disulfide cross-links. Introduction of β-mercaptoethanol (βME), emulating the reducing environment of the cytoplasm, results in the disassembly of the DM-labeled VLPs. The most effective DM binds VLPs slowly, destabilizes them more than other DMs, and leads to rapid disassembly; with this DM, labeling as few as 50% of available sites led to disassembly. Cargo-loaded DM-labeled VLPs also showed complete disassembly when incubated with βME. This work outlines a strategy for future development of VLPs as nanocontainers that are responsive to the environment.

title: Streamlining Hepatitis C Treatment: Implementation of a Clinical Pharmacist‐Driven Medication Management Program
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Hepatitis C virus (HCV) affects over 3.9 million individuals in the United States and is effectively treated with direct‐acting antiviral (DAA) agents. Clinical pharmacists (CPs) may be the ideal provider to bridge gaps in HCV care by selecting appropriate therapy following drug–drug interaction (DDI) review, navigating access barriers, and supporting adherence. Although CP involvement in HCV care has demonstrated clinical value, there is limited literature describing CP workflows, patient interventions, and CP‐led programs that support patients from treatment initiation through sustained virologic response at 12 weeks (SVR12). This study aims to quantify and categorize CP‐driven enrollments in a Hepatitis C Clinical Program (HCCP) and assess its impact on patient safety, operational, and clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective descriptive study evaluates a CP‐driven HCCP within a health system specialty pharmacy (HSSP) from May 6, 2024 to March 6, 2025. Patients with a referral to the CP for HCV treatment selection, or external patients with a DAA claim at the HSSP, were eligible for enrollment in the program. The HCCP consisted of six points of clinical care: CP therapy selection, medication access and order placement, prescription triage and patient education, follow‐up throughout treatment, intervention support, and laboratory monitoring through SVR12. Results A total of 122 patients were enrolled in the HCCP. Most patients were treatment‐naïve (90%) and non‐cirrhotic (79%). DDIs were identified in 57% of patients, with statin therapy being the most common (46%). Time‐to‐treatment was 4 days or less for 76% of patients, with an 88% HSSP prescription capture rate. A 97% SVR12 rate was achieved, and 92% of patients completed therapy on time. Conclusion This study highlights the role of the CP in HCV care and their impact on patient safety and clinical and operational outcomes. Results support further development of CP‐driven practice changes and support the implementation of a similar program within other HSSPs.

title: Hepatitis aguda de patrón hepatocelular asociada a infección primaria por virus de Epstein-Barr en una mujer inmunocompetente: reporte de caso
abstract: Introducción: La afectación hepática asociada a infección aguda por virus de Epstein-Barr es frecuente, aunque generalmente cursa con elevaciones leves y autolimitadas de las aminotransferasas. La hepatitis aguda clínicamente manifiesta como forma predominante de presentación constituye una manifestación menos habitual y puede representar un reto diagnóstico. Presentación del caso: Mujer de 25 años, inmunocompetente, con antecedente de hipotiroidismo primario y síndrome ovárico metabólico poliendócrino, quien presentó síndrome febril de 12 días de evolución asociado a dolor en hipocondrio derecho. Durante su evaluación se documentó leucocitosis con linfocitosis absoluta marcada, hepatoesplenomegalia y elevación significativa de aminotransferasas con patrón predominantemente hepatocelular (AST 417 U/L, ALT 833 U/L), bilirrubinas normales y función sintética hepática conservada. Inicialmente se consideraron diversas etiologías infecciosas y hepatobiliares; sin embargo, la presencia de hepatoesplenomegalia y linfocitosis orientó la sospecha hacia infección por VEB. Los estudios serológicos mostraron anticuerpos anti-VCA IgM y anti-VCA IgG positivos, con EBNA negativo, compatibles con infección aguda por VEB. Se descartaron infección por VIH, hepatitis B y hepatitis C. La tomografía abdominal evidenció hepatomegalia y esplenomegalia sin datos de obstrucción biliar. La paciente recibió tratamiento de soporte, con evolución clínica favorable y descenso progresivo de las alteraciones hematológicas y bioquímicas durante la hospitalización y el seguimiento ambulatorio. Conclusiones: La infección aguda por VEB debe considerarse dentro del diagnóstico diferencial de pacientes jóvenes con síndrome febril, hepatoesplenomegalia, linfocitosis y hepatitis aguda, incluso en ausencia de las manifestaciones clásicas de mononucleosis infecciosa. El reconocimiento oportuno de esta entidad puede contribuir a orientar adecuadamente el abordaje diagnóstico diferencial.

title: Blood-based PAaM score for predicting HCC risk in patients withHBV-related advanced fibrosis receiving nucleos(t)ide analogtherapy
abstract: Introduction: A composite score of clinical and molecular biomarkers, PAaM score, was associated with the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in advanced fibrosis in two independent large-scale phase 3 biomarker studies in the US; however, Asian patients and those with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection receiving nucleos(t)ide analog (NUC) therapy were markedly underrepresented. Methods: This study retrospectively analyzed 291 patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis prospectively enrolled at three tertiary-care centers in Japan. All patients had received NUCs for at least six months. The PAaM score was calculated by integrating the PLSec molecular biomarker panel, serum AFP, and the aMAP score. Patients were stratified into high-, intermediate-, and low-risk groups using pre-defined cut-offs. The primary analysis was the association of PAaM risk groups with incident HCC, accounting for competing mortality. In secondary analyses, performance was compared with aMAP, PAGE-B, and modified PAGE-B, mainly using the time-dependent area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Results: During a median follow-up of 8.3 years, 35 patients developed HCC. PAaM classified 8%, 29%, and 63% of patients into high-, intermediate-, and low-risk groups, respectively. The HCC incidence rates were 4.26, 2.71, and 0.82 per 100 person-years for high-, intermediate-, and low-risk patients, respectively (P = 0.003). The PAaM score was significantly associated with incident HCC, with a sub-distribution hazard ratio of 4.68 (95% CI 1.87 – 11.7) for high-risk versus low-risk patients. PAaM achieved the numerically highest AUPRC (0.21 at 3 years, 3.8-fold above the event prevalence). Conclusion: The PAaM score was externally validated as a risk stratification biomarker in Japanese patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis receiving NUC therapy.

title: Longitudinal fibrosis-4 monitoring: A promising approach for hepatocellular carcinoma risk stratification in treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis C
abstract: A substantial proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection remain untreated worldwide, sustaining a cumulative and age-dependent risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, particularly in resource-limited settings. Conventional risk stratification relies on baseline “snapshots” of fibrosis stage and single-time-point biomarkers, which may fail to capture the dynamic biology of fibrogenesis and carcinogenesis. In a long-term retrospective cohort of treatment-naïve patients with chronic hepatitis C virus published in the World Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology , Li et al reported that a 3-year increase in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index (ΔFIB-4 ≥ 1.0) independently predicted subsequent hepatocellular carcinoma (adjusted hazard ratio approximately 2.7), with the increasing trajectory group exhibiting a high long-term cumulative incidence. These findings suggest that longitudinal biomarker trajectories may refine long-term risk stratification beyond baseline staging, although the timing and actionable thresholds require prospective validation. Biologically, progressive increases in FIB-4 may reflect ongoing extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammation-driven microenvironmental shifts, and vascular alterations that promote tumor development. However, interpretation must account for age-related score drift, biological variability, and nonhepatic confounding. We propose a pragmatic framework integrating threshold-crossing and slope-based monitoring, combining serial FIB-4 with alpha-fetoprotein and key demographic modifiers. High-risk longitudinal patterns may warrant the use of confirmatory elastography and the consideration of intensified surveillance, pending prospective validation. Prospective studies are needed to standardize longitudinal cutoffs and validate clinical implementation.

title: First Molecular Detection of Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) RNA in Red Deer from Piedmont and Lombardy Regions (Italy): Potential Implications for Zoonotic Transmission
abstract: Paslahepevirus balayani (hepatitis E virus, HEV) is the causative agent of hepatitis E, a zoonotic disease of global public health concern. In Europe, human infections are mainly associated with genotype 3 (HEV-3), frequently linked to the consumption of raw or undercooked meat and meat products. Although pigs and wild boars are recognized as the main HEV reservoirs, the epidemiological role of deer remains unclear. This study investigated HEV RNA occurrence and genetic characteristics in red deer (Cervus elaphus) hunted in Piedmont and Lombardy, Italy. A total of 170 liver samples and 40 paired muscle samples from a subset of the same animals were analysed using touchdown RT-PCR followed by touchdown hemi-nested PCR. HEV RNA was detected in 22/170 liver samples (12.94%; 95% CI: 8.70–18.82%) and 3/40 muscle samples (7.50%; 95% CI: 2.58–19.86%). Partial HEV sequences were successfully obtained from 19 liver samples, and all were assigned to genotype 3 subtype 3c (HEV-3c). The three PCR-positive muscle samples were not sequence-confirmed. To our knowledge, this is the first molecular detection of HEV RNA in red deer from the sampled areas of Piedmont and Lombardy. These findings provide new data on HEV circulation in red deer in Northern Italy and highlight potential implications for food safety and public health.

title: EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DYNAMICS AND CLINICAL-DEMOGRAPHIC CHARACTERISTICS OF HEPATITIS C IN A POPULATION FROM SOUTHERN ROMANIA: A RETROSPECTIVE STUDY (2021–2024)
abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a major public health challenge. This retrospective study evaluated the seroprevalence of anti-HCV antibodies in a sample of 5346 patients tested in Alexandria (Teleorman County) between 2021 and 2024 using laboratoryenzyme immunoassays. The overall seropositivity rate was 1.53 % (82 cases), with no significant differences between females and males (1,70 % vs. 1,11%, p = 0,1417; OR = 1,54). Age distribution indicated a zero prevalence in the 18–34 age group (0.00 %) and a peakvalue of 3.70 % in the ≥65 age group (p = 2,75 × 10-14), confirming the persistence of a cohort effect. Temporal dynamics demonstrated a stable annual rate (1.89% in 2021, 1.40 % in 2022, 1.55 % in 2023, and 1.59 % in 2024, p = 0.9262), highlighting the need for continuedpopulation screening campaigns and sustained access to DAA therapies.

title: Expression Levels of miR-155 and miR-223 in Iraqi Patients with Hepatitis C Virus Infection
abstract: This study investigated the expression of miR-155 and miR-223 in Iraqi patients with acute and chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection to explore their potential roles in immune modulation and as biomarkers. A total of 242 individuals suspected of HCV infection were screened, of whom 40 were HCV RNA-positive and classified into acute (n=20) and chronic (n=20) infection groups. Twenty healthy controls were also included. Participants were recruited from the Hepatology and Gastroenterology Teaching Hospital in Baghdad, Iraq. Expression levels of miR-155 and miR-223 were measured using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), normalized to GAPDH, and calculated using the 2^−ΔΔCt method. MiR-155 expression was significantly higher in acute (3.05 ± 0.35) and chronic (3.82 ± 0.34) HCV groups than in healthy controls (1.34 ± 0.19). MiR-223 expression was significantly higher in chronic HCV infection (2.35 ± 0.37) than in acute infection (1.55 ± 0.22) and healthy controls (1.10 ± 0.11). These findings indicate that miR-155 is upregulated in both acute and chronic HCV infection, whereas miR-223 shows greater expression in chronic infection. Both miRNAs may contribute to immune modulation during HCV infection and warrant further investigation as potential biomarkers of disease progression.
journal: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF CLINICAL PATHOLOGY AND MEDICAL LABORATORY

abstract: Pemeriksaan triple eliminasi merupakan upaya deteksi dini HIV, sifilis, dan hepatitis B pada ibu hamil serta pencegahan penularan dari ibu kepada bayi. Namun, kepatuhan ibu hamil masih belum optimal dan dapat dipengaruhi oleh kurangnya pengetahuan, sikap yang kurang positif, serta minimnya dukungan suami. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui faktor-faktor yang berhubungan dengan kepatuhan ibu hamil dalam pemeriksaan triple eliminasi di Puskesmas Payung Sekaki Kota Pekanbaru Tahun 2026. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif analitik dengan desain cross sectional. Populasi berjumlah 149 ibu hamil dengan sampel 60 responden yang dipilih menggunakan purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner dan dianalisis secara univariat serta bivariat menggunakan uji Chi-Square. Hasil univariat menunjukkan 38 responden (63,3%) patuh melakukan pemeriksaan triple eliminasi, 37 responden (61,7%) memiliki pengetahuan baik, 42 responden (70,0%) memiliki sikap positif, dan 32 responden (53,3%) memperoleh dukungan suami yang tidak mendukung. Hasil bivariat menunjukkan terdapat hubungan signifikan antara pengetahuan (p=0,000; OR=29,700), sikap (p=0,004; OR=6,400), dan dukungan suami (p=0,000; OR=12,179) dengan kepatuhan pemeriksaan triple eliminasi. Disimpulkan bahwa pengetahuan, sikap, dan dukungan suami berhubungan signifikan dengan kepatuhan ibu hamil dalam melakukan pemeriksaan triple eliminasi. Peneliti selanjutnya disarankan mengkaji faktor lain, seperti dukungan tenaga kesehatan, akses pelayanan, motivasi, dan keterpaparan informasi.

title: Hepatitis C, Hearing Loss, and Healthcare Utilization Patterns, a Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES Data: 1999–2012
abstract: Objectives: Hearing loss is a chronic condition in the U.S. with diverse causes, including viral infections, and significantly affects quality of life. Despite the rising incidence of Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, research on its relationship with hearing loss remains limited. Early and consistent interactions with the healthcare system have been shown to improve outcomes in extrahepatic manifestations of HCV and enhance quality of life. Design: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of HCV history, identified via HCV antibody and RNA testing obtained by the mobile examination center, and hearing loss, measured by pure-tone audiometry, using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (1999–2004, 2011–2012) for adults aged 20 to 69. We utilized multivariable logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for important covariates. Results were stratified by degree of healthcare utilization. Results: Among 6705 participants, hearing loss prevalence was 27.7% in those with HCV versus 12.7% in those without. The adjusted OR for hearing loss in individuals with HCV was 1.81 (95% confidence interval: 1.06, 3.10). Notably, the magnitude of association between HCV history and hearing loss was higher in the low healthcare utilization group than in the high healthcare utilization group (aOR: 2.82 versus 0.72). Conclusions: Our findings suggest an association between HCV and hearing loss, with healthcare utilization modifying this relationship. This study fills a gap in the literature and highlights the need for increased clinical monitoring of hearing health in individuals who have had an HCV infection.

title: MARS-guided PubChem fingerprint selection and random forest classification of hepatitis C virus NS5B inhibitors with scaffold-independent prioritization of active chemotypes
abstract: Rational drug design accelerates early anti-hepatitis C discovery by learning the substructures that govern activity against the NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. This study proposes a two-stage model that couples multivariate adaptive regression splines with random forest classification to identify the PubChem fingerprints driving NS5B inhibition and to classify compounds as active or inactive. Multivariate adaptive regression splines capture non-linear main effects and pairwise interactions among binary fingerprints without distributional assumptions. After removal of training-set-constant fingerprints, 522 informative bits remained, from which the method selected 66 features. The analysis uses 578 non-redundant NS5B inhibitors curated from ChEMBL, comprising 412 active and 166 inactive compounds described by 881-bit PubChem substructure fingerprints. On a Bemis-Murcko scaffold-based external partition whose scaffolds are absent from training, random forest on the 66 selected bits reached a balanced accuracy of 84.4%, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.69, an area under the ROC curve of 0.91 and an average precision of 0.94, and it ranked all 20 of its top-scoring novel-scaffold compounds as truly active. Under stratified ten-fold cross-validation, with feature selection performed within each training fold, the same model reached a balanced accuracy of 89.0% and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.79, achieving the highest or near-highest performance among the classifiers tested with nearly unchanged accuracy despite the eightfold reduction in dimensionality. Structure-activity analysis identifies extended and branched aliphatic chains together with halogenated aromatic motifs as the substructures most enriched in NS5B inhibitory activity, and converts them into explicit rules for prioritizing active chemotypes.

title: HCV genotype-related serum lipid differences and their adjunctive value for identifying HIV/HCV co-infection in a Chinese male cohort
abstract: Background Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are associated with altered lipid profiles. This study examined lipid differences across infection groups and their associations with HCV genotype. An exploratory analysis evaluated models for identifying HCV co-infection among people with HIV. Methods This retrospective study included 551 male participants: 119 healthy controls, 120 with HCV mono-infection, 156 with HIV mono-infection, and 156 with HIV/HCV co-infection. Generalized linear models compared seven lipid parameters and tested interactions between HCV genotype and infection status. Models were adjusted for age, body mass index, glucose, albumin, fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations with HCV RNA levels. Three logistic regression models combined age with penalized regression-selected lipid parameters, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST), or both. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration curves, and bootstrap internal validation. Results All seven lipid parameters were lower in the HIV/HCV co-infection group than in the HIV mono-infection group after adjustment (all P < 0.05). Adjusted mean total cholesterol (TC) was 3.70 (95% CI: 3.59-3.83) versus 4.53 (4.44-4.63) mmol/L, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) was 2.05 (1.97-2.14) versus 2.65 (2.57-2.73) mmol/L. Significant interactions between HCV genotype and infection status were observed for TC and LDL-C ( P = 0.006; P = 0.008). In the co-infection group, genotype 3 had lower TC and LDL-C than genotypes 1 and 2, with adjusted means of 3.11 and 1.58 mmol/L, respectively. Neither parameter differed significantly across genotypes in HCV mono-infection. HCV RNA levels were not significantly associated with any lipid parameter. In the exploratory prediction analysis, the combined model had an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.977 (95% CI: 0.963-0.992), compared with 0.872 for the lipid model and 0.946 for the liver enzyme model. Its bootstrap-validated AUC was 0.975. Conclusion HIV/HCV co-infection was associated with marked reductions in serum lipid levels. Genotype-related differences in TC and LDL-C varied by HIV co-infection status. A model combining age, five lipid parameters, ALT, and AST may provide adjunctive information for identifying HCV co-infection among people with HIV.

title: Manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: la exposición ocupacional a la sangre, sobre todo por objetos punzocortantes, fue el principal riesgo para el personal. La vacunación contra la hepatitis B y la profilaxis posexposición fueron las medidas más eficaces frente a las infecciones sanguíneas. Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

Received 3 August, 2026; Accepted 13 October, 2026 Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d’Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)- positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication. This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg- positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888–1122 and 313–485). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%). Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia. Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection. INTRODUCTION Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most widespread infectious agents worldwide. An estimated 254 million people were living with chronic HBV infection in 2022, resulting in approximately 1.1 million deaths, while only 13% of carriers had been diagnosed and 3% had received treatment (World Health Organization [WHO], 2024). Sub-Saharan Africa bears a disproportionate share of this burden, with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence exceeding 8% in many areas and estimated at 9 to 12% among the general adult population in Côte d’Ivoire (WHO, 2021). A meta-analysis involving more than 3.5 million African blood donors reported a pooled HBsAg seroprevalence of 10.09% in West Africa, the highest among the continent’s five regions (Quintas et al., 2024). This substantial burden is consistent with findings indicating that HBsAg prevalence among blood donors at the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI) remained stable over two decades (Seri et al., 2018). Hepatitis delta virus (HDV), first described by Rizzetto in 1977 (Rizzetto et al., 1980), is a defective RNA virus that depends on HBV surface antigen for its replication and transmission. Consequently, HDV infection occurs only in HBsAg-positive individuals, either through simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection or through HDV superinfection in individuals with pre-existing chronic HBV infection. Approximately 90% of individuals with chronic HBV infection who acquire HDV superinfection progress to chronic HDV infection, whereas simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection is usually resolved, although serological markers may persist without ongoing viral replication (Rizzetto et al., 2021). This distinction is important when comparing anti-HDV antibody prevalence, which indicates previous or current exposure, with HDV RNA positivity, which provides evidence of active viral replication. HBV/HDV coinfection is associated with more severe liver disease than HBV monoinfection, increasing the risk of cirrhosis by approximately two- to three-fold and the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma by approximately two-fold. Cirrhosis may develop in 70 to 80% of affected patients within 5 to 10 years (Fattovich et al., 2000; Negro, 2014; Noureddin and Gish, 2014). Globally, an estimated 15–20 million HBsAg-positive individuals are thought to have HDV infection, although these estimates may be inflated when subpopulation weighting is not adequately considered (Rizzetto, 2015; Polaris Observatory Collaborators, 2024). Data on HDV infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain limited and heterogeneous. Reported anti-HDV seroprevalence ranges from approximately 7% in pooled estimates for West Africa to more than 25% in Central Africa (Stockdale et al., 2017). Country-specific estimates also vary considerably, ranging from 1 to 54% in Cameroon (Besombes et al., 2020), 7 to 22% in Mauritania (Mansour et al., 2012; Lunel-Fabiani et al., 2013), and 8 to 9% in Nigeria (Opaleye et al., 2016). In Senegal, active HDV replication confirmed by RNA testing was detected in 61.5% of anti-HDV-seropositive individuals, despite an Dechi et al. 21 overall anti-HDV seroprevalence of only 1.5% (Wembulua et al., 2025). These findings illustrate the distinction between antibody-based estimates of exposure and RNA- based evidence of active infection. Before the present study, published data on HBV/HDV coinfection in Côte d’Ivoire were very limited. Regarding treatment, pegylated interferon had long remained the principal therapeutic option, despite its limited efficacy (Wedemeyer et al., 2011). The approval of bulevirtide by the European Medicines Agency introduced a new treatment option for chronic HDV infection (Asselah et al., 2020), although access remains limited in resource-constrained settings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of active HDV RNA replication among HBsAg-positive blood donors receiving follow-up care at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the CNTSCI, using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two distinct HDV genomic regions. The secondary objectives were to describe the sociodemographic and virological characteristics of this population and examine the relationship between HDV RNA positivity and HBV viraemia. MATERIALS AND METHODS Study setting and design This was a cross-sectional, descriptive and analytical study conducted in March 2021 at the CNTSCI, specifically within the CMSDS. Laboratory analyses were performed at the molecular biology platform of the Immunology Laboratory of the UFR of Medical Sciences (UFR-SM) at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny. Study population, sampling strategy and inclusion criteria The target population consisted of voluntary blood donors regularly followed at the CMSDS with confirmed positive HBsAg serology. Recruitment used a non-probabilistic, exhaustive convenience sampling strategy: all HBsAg-positive donors attending scheduled CMSDS follow-up visits during the study period and satisfying the inclusion criteria were consecutively invited to participate. Inclusion criteria were: (i) being a voluntary blood donor followed at the CMSDS; (ii) presenting a confirmed positive HBsAg result; and (iii) having provided consent to participate in the study. Donors whose biological samples were insufficient or of poor quality were excluded. Collection and pre-treatment of biological samples Blood samples were collected from each participant in Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) tubes. Study variables Sociodemographic data collected included sex, age, and educational level. Virological and therapeutic data comprised HBV viral load, antiviral treatment status (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate [TDF] or no treatment), and the qualitative HDV RNA (nested RT-PCR) result. Statistical analysis Data were entered using Microsoft Excel software and analysed using SPSS V27 statistical software International Business Machines Corporation (IBM). Qualitative variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. Quantitative variables were described using the mean and standard deviation (SD). HDV RNA prevalence was calculated with its 95% confidence interval (95% CI), computed on the denominator of donors with an available HBV viral-load result, as distinct from the full enrolled cohort. Associations were tested using the chi-squared test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate given expected cell counts, with statistical significance set at P < 0.05. No a sample size calculation was performed. Ethical considerations This study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki. Data were collected anonymously, and all participants provided written informed consent. The study forms part of the CNTSCI's epidemiological surveillance activities. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) RNA replication among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors in Côte d'Ivoire. Using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), HDV RNA was detected in two genomic regions. Of 51 donors, 43 had HBV DNA results, with 90.7% showing HDV RNA positivity. Notably, HDV RNA was detected in donors with suppressed HBV viraemia on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF). The study, based on a convenience sample, is hypothesis-generating and underscores the need for systematic HDV screening in chronic HBV patients. However, it does not provide population-level estimates due to its limited scope.

abstract_zh: 慢性丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 感染会加剧 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关肝病。在科特迪瓦,未对乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阳性献血者进行系统性筛查,大多数区域估计依赖于抗 HDV 血清学,这表明暴露但不活跃复制。本研究旨在确定 HBsAg 阳性献血者中 HDV RNA 复制阳性情况。科特迪瓦国家输血中心 (CNTSCI) 的献血者医疗随访中心 (CMSDS) 使用巢式逆转录聚合酶链式反应 (RT-PCR)。2021 年 3 月进行了一项基于非概率便利样本的横断面研究。通过针对两个基因组区域(核苷酸 888-1122 和 313-485)的巢式 RT-PCR 检测了 HDV RNA。51 名捐献者中其中,75% 为男性 (n = 38),平均年龄为 37 ± 9 岁。43 名捐献者 (84%) 可获得 HBV DNA 结果。其中,可检测到 HBV 病毒血症的 HDV RNA 阳性率为 88.9% (32/36),病毒载量无法检测到的患者为 100% (7/7),总体阳性率为 90.7% (39/43)。该数字仅适用于具有可用病毒载量数据的捐献者,而不是 51 名捐献者的全部 队列研究。在接受富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯 (TDF) 且 HBV 病毒血症受到抑制的捐献者中也检测到 HDV RNA。考虑到已经处于后续护理中的捐献者的方便样本,研究结果是假设生成而不是人群水平估计。这些结果支持更大规模的代表性研究和个体随访期间的系统性 HDV 筛查关键词:乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒(HBV/HDV)合并感染,巢式逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR),分子流行病学,方便样本,输血医学,西非。

title_original: Associations among family history of hepatitis B virus, baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and surface antigen clearance

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the associations between family history of hepatitis B virus, baseline hepatitis B surface antigen levels and surface antigen clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in China, focusing on patients with chronic hepatitis B who received pegylated interferon-α treatment. The study included a sample of patients with documented family history of hepatitis B virus and baseline HBsAg levels.
analysis.methods: The study utilized a retrospective cohort design, analyzing medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B. It assessed family history of hepatitis B virus, baseline HBsAg levels, and outcomes related to HBsAg clearance following pegylated interferon-α treatment.
analysis.main_results: The study found that family history of hepatitis B virus was significantly associated with a lower hazard of HBsAg clearance. Approximately 37% of this negative association was mediated by elevated baseline HBsAg levels.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as suggesting that patients with a family history of hepatitis B virus may have a reduced likelihood of achieving HBsAg clearance with pegylated interferon-α, potentially requiring lower baseline HBsAg levels to achieve similar outcomes as those without family history.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of personalized treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B patients based on their family history and baseline HBsAg levels, potentially improving therapeutic outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on medical records, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the associations between family history of hepatitis B virus, baseline hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels, and HBsAg clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B. A retrospective cohort study was conducted in China, analyzing medical records of patients who received pegylated interferon-α treatment. The results showed that family history of hepatitis B virus was significantly linked to a lower hazard of HBsAg clearance, with approximately 37% of this association mediated by elevated baseline HBsAg levels. The authors interpreted these findings as indicating that HBFH-positive patients may require lower baseline HBsAg levels to achieve comparable clearance rates to HBFH-negative patients. The study's findings may inform personalized treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B patients, considering their family history and baseline HBsAg levels. However, the study's retrospective design and reliance on medical records limit the confidence in its results, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于根据 慢性乙型肝炎 患者的家族史和基线 HBsAg 水平制定个性化 治疗 策略,从而有可能改善治疗结果。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对医疗记录的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

full_text: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a blood-borne virus that is nationally notifiable in Australia. Despite inclusion of the HBV vaccine in the childhood National Immunisation Program, local and overseas-acquired cases occur. An increase in newly acquired HBV cases in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024 prompted an outbreak investigation. Epidemiological analyses of demographics, disease onset, and risk factors were combined with laboratory investigations, including whole genome sequencing (WGS) for genotyping and phylogenetic analysis.Twenty newly acquired cases were included, with three additional cases investigated. Most cases were aged over 30 years (n = 18, 78%) and reported casual unprotected sex (n = 17, 74%); some were born overseas (n = 8, 33%) or used intravenous drugs (n = 7, 30%). Four had received at least three HBV vaccines, although timing of doses varied. Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were locally acquired sub-genotype A2 HBV. Three sub-genotype A2 clusters and one sub-genotype B3 cluster were identified.This study is one of the first in Australia to investigate a potential HBV outbreak using WGS. Although genetic diversity within individual patient samples (within-host sequence heterogeneity) complicated relatedness analyses and limited the assessment of transmission pathways, WGS complemented epidemiological methods, which had demonstrated few links. The increase in sub-genotype A2 cases was likely due to coincident introductions of multiple HBV strains into Perth with some limited local transmission. Acknowledgements The Master of Applied Epidemiology scholarship for RS is funded by the Boorloo Public Health Unit, Western Australia. No other funding was provided for this investigation.The authors wish to thank staff at the Boorloo Public Health Unit who undertake the public health follow up of hepatitis B in metropolitan Perth, and the Pathogen and Surveillance Unit and Molecular Diagnostics Section, PathWest for their assistance in the development of the whole genome sequencing assay. Funding The Master of Applied Epidemiology scholarship for RS is funded by the Boorloo Public Health Unit, Western Australia. No other funding was provided for this investigation. Data were collected under statutory public health powers for the purpose of communicable disease control in accordance with the Western Australian Public Health Act 2016 and Public Health Regulations 2017. Ethics approval for the use of these data for research purposes was granted by the Australian National University Human Research Ethics Committee (Reference: 2017/090). The HREC formally waived the requirement for individual patient consent to participate in accordance with Sect. 2.3 of the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research. title_original: Investigation of a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B in a metropolitan setting: insights from whole genome sequencing

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B cases in metropolitan Perth to understand the potential outbreak and transmission dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An outbreak investigation was conducted in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024, including 20 newly acquired cases and three additional cases for further analysis.
analysis.methods: Epidemiological analyses of demographics, disease onset, and risk factors were combined with laboratory investigations, including whole genome sequencing (WGS) for genotyping and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis.main_results: Most cases were aged over 30 years (n = 18, 78%) and reported casual unprotected sex (n = 17, 74%); some were born overseas (n = 8, 33%) or used intravenous drugs (n = 7, 30%). Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were locally acquired sub-genotype A2 HBV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified three sub-genotype A2 clusters and one sub-genotype B3 cluster, highlighting the role of WGS in complementing traditional epidemiological methods to better understand transmission patterns.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the increase in sub-genotype A2 cases may be due to multiple introductions of HBV strains into Perth, with limited local transmission, informing targeted public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Genetic diversity within individual patient samples complicated relatedness analyses, and the study's results were limited by the small sample size and the lack of clear epidemiological links.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B cases in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024. The outbreak was analyzed using epidemiological data and whole genome sequencing (WGS) to determine transmission dynamics. Most cases were over 30 years old and reported casual unprotected sex, with some born overseas or using intravenous drugs. Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were sub-genotype A2 HBV, and three clusters of this genotype were identified, along with one sub-genotype B3 cluster. The study suggests that the increase in cases may result from multiple introductions of HBV strains into Perth, with limited local transmission. While WGS provided insights, within-host sequence heterogeneity complicated relatedness analyses. The findings have implications for public health surveillance and intervention strategies in the region.

title_original: Advances in the immunological basis and therapeutic strategies for functional cure of chronic hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the immunological mechanisms underlying chronic hepatitis B and identify therapeutic strategies for achieving a functional cure. The background highlights that persistent viral reservoirs and sustained antigen-driven immune dysfunction are major constraints in the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This review article provides an overview of the immunological basis and therapeutic strategies for the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B. It outlines the mechanisms of immune dysfunction and their implications for treatment approaches, with no specific study population or design described.
analysis.methods: The review synthesizes human clinical evidence and discusses the potential of biomarker-guided stratification and rational sequencing of therapies to balance efficacy against immune-mediated liver injury.
analysis.main_results: The review identifies key mechanisms such as hepatitis B virus-specific T-cell exhaustion, B-cell dysfunction, hepatic immune tolerance, innate immune dysregulation, and metabolic and gut-liver axis remodeling as constraints to achieving a functional cure. It also outlines emerging therapeutic strategies including pegylated interferon, therapeutic vaccination, immune checkpoint modulation, and innate immune activation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that understanding these mechanisms can inform the development of a staged strategy for durable HBsAg loss. The novelty lies in linking these immunological mechanisms to therapeutic approaches for functional cure.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the design of future studies and therapeutic strategies aimed at achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B by addressing immune dysfunction and viral reservoirs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a review and does not present original clinical data, which limits the strength of the evidence. The confidence in the findings is moderate as they are based on existing literature rather than new experimental results.

analysis.summary_en: This review article explores the immunological mechanisms that hinder the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B, emphasizing persistent viral reservoirs and sustained antigen-driven immune dysfunction. It outlines key mechanisms such as T-cell exhaustion, B-cell dysfunction, hepatic immune tolerance, innate immune dysregulation, and metabolic and gut-liver axis remodeling. The authors propose emerging therapeutic strategies, including pegylated interferon, therapeutic vaccination, immune checkpoint modulation, and innate immune activation, to address these challenges. The review highlights the importance of biomarker-guided stratification and rational treatment sequencing to balance efficacy with the risk of immune-mediated liver injury. While the study provides valuable insights into the immunological basis of chronic hepatitis B, its findings are based on existing literature, limiting the strength of the evidence. The review serves as a foundation for future research and therapeutic development in the field of hepatitis B.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探索 慢性乙型肝炎 背后的免疫学机制,并确定实现 功能性治愈 的治疗策略。背景强调,持续的病毒储存宿主和持续的抗原驱动的免疫功能障碍是慢性乙型肝炎的功能性治愈的主要限制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本综述文章概述了 慢性乙型肝炎 的免疫学基础和治疗策略。它概述了免疫功能障碍的机制及其对 治疗 方法的影响,但没有描述具体的研究人群或设计。
elements_zh.methods: 该综述综合了人类临床证据,并讨论了生物标志物引导的分层和合理的治疗排序以平衡免疫介导的肝损伤疗效的潜力。
elements_zh.main_results: 该综述确定了 乙型肝炎病毒 特异性 T 细胞耗竭、B 细胞功能障碍、肝脏免疫耐受、先天免疫失调以及代谢和肠肝轴重塑等关键机制作为实现 功能性治愈 的限制。它还概述了新兴的治疗策略,包括聚乙二醇干扰素、治疗性 疫苗接种、免疫检查点调节和先天免疫激活。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,了解这些机制可以为制定持久 HBsAg 消失的分阶段策略提供信息。新颖之处在于将这些免疫机制与 功能性治愈 的治疗方法联系起来。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为未来研究和治疗策略的设计提供信息,旨在通过解决免疫功能障碍和病毒 储存宿主 来实现 慢性乙型肝炎 的 功能性治愈。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项综述,不提供原始临床数据,这限制了证据的强度。研究结果的可信度中等,因为它们是基于现有文献而不是新的实验结果。

title: Semi-quantitative ultrasound scoring reveals hepatic structural recovery and immune modulation during tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.

title_zh: 半定量超声评分揭示慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)在接受替诺福韦艾拉酚胺治疗期间肝脏结构恢复和免疫调节
source_body_en: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。方法 入选了100例接受TAF单药治疗(25 mg/天)至少24个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者进行回顾性分析。在基线、12个月和24个月时计算了包含肝脏回声、包膜轮廓、边缘形态、血管清晰度、门静脉直径(PVD)、脾脏厚度(ST)和脾静脉血流速度(SVV)的七参数半定量超声评分。同时测量了血清乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)脱氧核糖核酸(DNA)、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)、天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)以及外周T细胞亚群,包括分化簇3阳性(CD3+)、CD4+、CD8+ T细胞、CD4+/CD8+比值和自然杀伤(NK)细胞活性。分析了超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的相关性。结果 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。CD4+ T细胞比例和CD4+/CD8+比值增加,而CD8+ T细胞比例下降;NK细胞活性从42.7 ± 7.3%上升至52.4 ± 6.2%(P < 0.05)。超声评分与ALT(r = 0.56)和AST(r = 0.47)呈正相关,与CD4+/CD8+比值(r = −0.46)和NK细胞活性(r = −0.38)呈负相关(所有P < 0.01)。结论 这些发现表明,TAF不仅抑制病毒复制并使肝酶正常化,还促进可测量的肝脏结构改善,这体现在半定量超声评分的下降。超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的强相关性支持其作为非侵入性影像生物标志物用于监测治疗疗效和肝脏修复的潜力。
